ultimate_skill.description: Vorlag channels the full fury of the earthcore within him. He leaps into the air and crashes down at a targeted location, creating a massive volcanic eruption. The impact zone becomes a miniature labyrinth of flame and molten rock—enemies inside are continuously damaged and slowed, their vision obscured by smoke and ash. Vorlag himself becomes a walking inferno within this zone, his attacks erupting with bonus magma damage and his speed unaffected by the treacherous terrain. As the flames subside, only Vorlag remains standing amidst the cooling stone, the echo of his roar lingering like thunder.

title: The Corrupted Enforcer
lore: Markus Vex was once a decorated police captain in the corrupt metropolis of Ashvale City, a man who genuinely believed in justice until the system he served showed him that power, not righteousness, was the true currency of the realm. After witnessing his partner murdered by a crime lord who bought his freedom with political connections, Markus's faith in the law shattered. In his moment of darkest despair, a shadowy figure from Kishima appeared—a demon of the Corrupted Machine Gods who offered him power in exchange for his soul. Markus accepted without hesitation. The transformation fused his police gear with demonic technology: his standard-issue baton became a conduit for hellish electricity, his uniform absorbed the essence of fire itself, and from the depths of his corrupted armor emerged a shield of pure energy three times his size. Now, Captain Vex walks the line between law enforcement and criminality, using his badge as cover while he dispenses his own brutal brand of justice. He answers to no department, no judge, no law but his own. The citizens of Ashvale whisper that when you see a man in a red and brown police hat with eyes that glow like embers, justice is coming—but it might burn you alive.
description: Captain Markus Vex cuts an imposing figure of corrupted authority, a man whose very presence screams that the law has been twisted into something monstrous. His face is a study in harsh angles and shadowed cynicism—a strong, square jaw perpetually set in a grim line, high cheekbones that catch the orange glow of his own fires, and a straight nose with a slight crook from a long-ago break that never healed properly. His eyes are his most terrifying feature: once a piercing ice-blue, they now burn with an inner molten orange-red fire that spills from his irises like embers from a forge, the pupils contracted to vertical slits that mark his demonic transformation. Deep-set and constantly narrowed with suspicion or contempt, these eyes miss nothing and forgive nothing. His hair is a short, practical cut of dark auburn brown, graying at the temples, always slightly disheveled beneath his signature hat. That hat is a traditional police peaked cap, but corrupted—the base is deep burgundy leather with a brown patent leather brim, and where a standard badge would be, a demonic symbol of a flaming scale sits, crafted from tarnished brass that seems to pulse with inner heat. His upper body is encased in a heavily modified police duty uniform that resembles tactical armor more than simple fabric. The base is a deep crimson-red, almost blood-colored, Kevlar-weave tactical shirt with a high mandarin collar that protects his neck. Over this, he wears a fitted brown leather vest reinforced with dark bronze plates that cover his chest, shoulders, and upper arms. The vest is crisscrossed with leather straps and silver buckles, each one holding spare ammunition for his secondary weapons or small vials of incendiary gel. His shoulders are capped with angular bronze pauldrons etched with flame patterns that glow faintly when he channels his power. From his left shoulder, a tactical harness extends across his chest, holding his primary weapon—the 'Judgment Baton'—in a quick-draw holster on his right hip. The baton itself is a masterpiece of corrupted technology: when collapsed, it's a simple 12-inch handle of dark red alloy wrapped in black leather, but when extended with a flick of his wrist, it becomes a 3-foot shaft that crackles with red-orange electricity, the energy arcing between segmented metal sections like captured lightning. At its tip, the electricity concentrates into a glowing orange ball that can deliver devastating shocks or, when he channels his fire affinity, ignite into explosive firestorms. His right hand is covered by a fingerless tactical glove of brown leather with reinforced bronze knuckles, allowing him to grip the baton's energy without being burned. His left forearm bears a wide bronze bracer, intricately carved with demonic runes that pulse with orange light—this is the source of his shield. When activated, a massive hexagonal energy barrier of translucent orange and red erupts from the bracer, expanding to three times his size, covered in crackling electricity and swirling fire patterns. The shield can protect him from any attack while simultaneously burning anything that gets too close. His lower body is clad in matching deep crimson tactical pants, reinforced at the knees with brown leather and bronze plates, tucked into heavy black combat boots with thick treads and steel toes. A wide brown leather belt with a massive brass buckle shaped like a flaming badge cinches his waist, holding additional pouches and a back-up collapsible baton. The entire ensemble radiates an aura of corrupted authority—faint waves of heat shimmer around him constantly, and occasional sparks of red electricity leap from his baton or shield bracer. When he moves, it's with the deliberate, heavy tread of a man who knows he is judge, jury, and executioner, and the air around him smells faintly of ozone and burning leather.

story.part1: Markus Vex joined the Ashvale City Police Department at twenty-two, fresh out of the academy with top honors and a burning desire to make a difference. He rose through the ranks quickly, his dedication and natural leadership earning him the captain's badge by thirty-five. He was respected by his officers and feared by criminals—a man of principle who believed that the law was the only thing standing between civilization and chaos.
story.part2: His partner of ten years, Detective Elena Reyes, was his closest friend and most trusted ally. Together, they had taken down some of the city's most dangerous criminals. When they finally gathered enough evidence to arrest Silas Korr, the crime lord who controlled Ashvale's underworld, Markus thought justice was finally at hand. But Korr's political connections ran deeper than anyone knew. The night before the arrest, Markus received a phone call: Elena had been found dead in her apartment, killed in what officials called a 'botched burglary.' Markus knew the truth. Korr had bought her life with campaign contributions.
story.part3: For three months, Markus tried to build a case against Korr through legal channels. Every door was closed. Every witness recanted. Every piece of evidence disappeared. The system he had devoted his life to serving had become his enemy. On the anniversary of Elena's death, Markus stood on the rooftop of the precinct, staring down at the city below, and felt something inside him break.
story.part4: It was then that a figure emerged from the shadows—a being of metal and flame, one of the Corrupted Machine Gods from Kishima. It offered Markus power: the ability to deliver justice that no politician could buy off, no lawyer could delay, no judge could dismiss. The price was his soul. Markus accepted without hesitation. The transformation was agony and ecstasy as demonic energy fused with his police gear, his very body becoming a weapon of corrupted law enforcement.
story.part5: The next morning, Silas Korr was found dead in his penthouse, electrocuted and burned beyond recognition. The security footage showed only a figure in a red and brown police hat, eyes glowing like embers, walking through walls of fire. Markus Vex continued to report for duty, his badge still shining, his uniform still pressed. But everyone who looked into his eyes knew: Captain Vex was no longer a man. He was something far more dangerous.

title: The Abyssal Archmage
lore: Morgause was not born wicked—she was forged in the crucible of jealousy, her soul tempered by the fires of being second-born, second-seen, second-loved. Twin sister to Morgana, the celebrated prodigy of the Spire Academy, Morgause grew up in her sister's shadow, watching as their parents lavished praise on Morgana's every accomplishment while dismissing her own considerable talents as mere imitation. While Morgana was lauded as the brightest student in a millennium, Morgause was called 'promising'—a word that stung worse than any insult. The jealousy festered for decades, a slow poison that transformed admiration into hatred, love into bitter resentment. When Morgana performed her forbidden celestial summoning and merged with the cosmic entity, the event that made her sister a legend also cracked something fundamental in Morgause's psyche. She saw not triumph, but theft—Morgana had stolen the destiny that should have been hers. In her rage and despair, Morgause descended into the deepest archives of the Spire's forbidden section, seeking power that would not merely match her sister's, but eclipse it utterly. She found what she sought in texts older than the academy itself—tomes bound in the skin of leviathans, written in ink pressed from abyssal algae, describing pacts with entities from the lightless depths where even cosmic beings feared to tread. She summoned something from those depths—not a celestial, but a primordial water deity older than stars, a consciousness of crushing pressure and absolute cold that had slumbered since before light existed. It offered her power beyond mortal comprehension, power to drown worlds, in exchange for her service. Morgause accepted, and the transformation was agonizing ecstasy. Her body changed, her skin taking on a deep greenish-black sheen like abyssal waters, her eyes becoming pools of liquid darkness with swirling emerald light. Where Morgana had gained six magnificent wings of shadow and light, Morgause gained the ability to manifest water itself as armor, weapon, and servant. Now she hunts her sister not from hate alone, but from a twisted sense of cosmic justice—she believes Morgana's light-based power is an affront to the true darkness that birthed the universe. She has become an archmage of the abyss, commanding floods that can swallow cities, ice that can freeze time itself, and pressure so immense it can crush the soul. She is Morgause, the Abyssal Archmage, and she will drag her sister into the depths or die trying.
description: Morgause is the dark mirror of her sister Morgana, a vision of abyssal beauty that contrasts sharply with Morgana's celestial radiance. Where Morgana is all silvery-white and ethereal cyan, Morgause is deep verdant green and absolute black, a living embodiment of the lightless depths. Her face shares the same sharp elegant V-shape with high aristocratic cheekbones as her sister, but where Morgana's expression holds knowing arrogance, Morgause's face is twisted into a perpetual sneer of bitter contempt and wicked amusement. Her skin is pale with a distinct greenish-black undertone, like moonlight filtering through deep ocean water, giving her an ethereal yet unsettling appearance. Her eyes are her most devastating feature—they are deep pools of absolute black with swirling emerald green light that moves like bioluminescent algae in dark waters, holding the crushing pressure of the abyss and the cold amusement of one who has made peace with her own wickedness. A thin, precise gold monocle rests over her right eye, attached by an delicate gold chain that drapes over her cheek—the same as Morgana's, a cruel mockery of their shared past. Her hair is a magnificent cascade of deep emerald green with absolute black undertones, flowing in waves that seem to move with the slow, hypnotic grace of deep ocean currents, styled in the same voluminous waves as her sister but in colors of poison and shadow rather than light. On her head sits a witch's hat that mirrors Morgana's but in reversed colors—where her sister's is violet-purple with gold, Morgause's is deep abyssal green with a wide, slightly tattered brim of absolute black, the tall twisted peak leaning backward, heavily adorned with tarnished silver filigree and glowing emerald gems. A golden crescent moon ornament sits at the base of the crown, identical to Morgana's but tarnished and blackened as if by deep-sea corrosion. Her attire is a study in contrast and corruption. She wears a form-fitting sleeveless leotard base in deep iridescent green and black that highlights every curve, the fabric seeming to shift and ripple like water. Layered under a majestic floor-length trailing coat of deep abyssal green exterior lined with rich velvety black, the coat's hem trimmed with black feathers and stylized wave patterns that seem to move. Her arms are encased in dark metallic viridian gauntlets that flare into wicked black wing-like guards at the elbows, each gauntlet etched with patterns of drowning souls and abyssal creatures. Her legs are bare, one clad in a sheer black stocking on the right leg while the left remains bare, showing skin with the same greenish-black undertone, and on her feet she wears elegant high-heeled sabatons resembling the claws of deep-sea predators, the heels shaped like curved talons. But her most magnificent and terrifying feature is her replacement for wings—instead of feathered wings, Morgause is perpetually surrounded by floating constructs of living water. Three massive, serpentine water tendrils constantly orbit her body, each one twenty feet long, formed of swirling deep green and absolute black water that seems to have a life of its own. These tendrils can solidify into armor, lash out as weapons, or simply hover menacingly, dripping abyssal water that evaporates into black mist. In her right hand, she delicately holds a slender golden wand pulsing with concentrated viridian energy—identical to Morgana's but with green light instead of pink-purple. In her left hand, she commands a massive floating grimoire bound in what appears to be leviathan leather, deep green-black with silver clasps shaped like gaping maws, its pages overflowing with raw abyssal magic that drips like liquid shadow, the book alive with power and whispers of the drowned. Her entire form radiates an aura of crushing malevolence—the air around her feels heavy, wet, impossibly dense, and those near her feel the inexplicable urge to gasp for breath as if drowning. She is Morgause, and she has made a pact with the deepest darkness.

story.part1: Morgause's earliest memories are of watching. Watching her sister Morgana receive praise, watching their parents' faces light up at Morgana's accomplishments, watching the world celebrate her twin while she stood in the shadows. They were identical in appearance as children—both with the same sharp features, the same potential—but something in their souls was different from the beginning. Morgana burned with confidence and ambition; Morgause burned with the colder fire of observation and patience. She learned to smile when she wanted to scream, to congratulate when she wanted to curse.
story.part2: At the Spire Academy, the separation became absolute. Morgana was the star, the prodigy, the one whispered about in hallowed tones. Morgause was 'Morgana's sister'—a label that followed her everywhere, a brand that marked her as derivative, secondary, less. She studied just as hard, mastered spells just as quickly, but her accomplishments were always measured against her sister's, always found wanting. The teachers meant well, perhaps, but their constant comparisons carved wounds that never healed.
story.part3: When Morgana broke into the restricted library and performed the forbidden celestial summoning, Morgause was the one who discovered the aftermath. She found the ritual circle, the scattered scrolls, the lingering traces of power that would transform her sister into something beyond mortal. And she felt something she had never allowed herself to fully acknowledge: pure, incandescent hatred. Not for what Morgana had done, but for what she had become—a being of light and wonder, while Morgause remained merely talented, merely promising, merely Morgana's sister.
story.part4: The descent into the forbidden archives was a pilgrimage of self-destruction. Morgause delved deeper than any student had gone in centuries, past wards that would have killed the unprepared, past warnings written in blood and despair. She found the Abyssal Texts in a chamber that should not exist, a room where water defied gravity and the air itself was thick enough to drown in. She read the pacts, learned the rituals, and understood the price. She summoned the Drowned One, the primordial consciousness that had existed before light, that had watched the first stars ignite from the crushing depths. It offered her power to rival any celestial, power to command the abyss itself, in exchange for her service and her soul. Morgause accepted without a moment's hesitation.
story.part5: The transformation was a death and rebirth. She felt her body dissolve into lightless depths and reform, piece by piece, her very cells saturated with abyssal energy. When she emerged, she was no longer Morgana's sister. She was Morgause, the Abyssal Archmage, and she had power that made her sister's celestial wings seem like candle flames. Her first act was to drown the Spire Academy's restricted section, erasing the texts that had made her and ensuring no other could follow her path. Her second act was to begin her hunt for Morgana—not from hate alone, but from a philosopher's conviction: light is a lie, a brief flicker in the eternal darkness, and she would prove it by extinguishing the brightest light she knew.

title: The Reluctant Archsage
nickname: Bearded Arbiter of the Umbradra Legacy
lore: The Umbradra family has produced many legendary mages across the millennia—Morgana and Morgause being only the most recent in a long line of arcane prodigies. But among all the Umbradra bloodline, one name is whispered with a mixture of awe and confusion: Flient Umbradra, the cousin who could have been the greatest of them all, yet chose to be nothing at all. Born thirty years before the twins, Flient displayed such terrifying magical aptitude as a child that the family elders believed he would ascend to godhood before his twentieth year. By twelve, he had mastered all eight schools of magic. By fifteen, he had begun creating his own spells—spells that even the oldest archmages could not comprehend. By eighteen, he had achieved something no mortal had ever accomplished: he had looked upon the fundamental laws of reality, understood them completely, and found them... boring. While his younger cousins Morgana and Morgause competed for attention and power, Flient quietly withdrew from the Umbradra estates. He had seen the pinnacle of magical achievement and realized that power, in itself, was meaningless without purpose. He abandoned his studies, left his family, and settled in a small village in the remote countryside, where he took up farming. For twelve years, the greatest wizard of his age lived as a simple farmer, growing vegetables, tending sheep, and occasionally helping villagers with minor problems using magic so subtle they thought it was just good luck. He married a local woman named Elara, a baker's daughter with no magical talent whatsoever, and for the first time in his life, he knew peace. They had a daughter, Mira, who inherited her mother's warm heart and her father's brilliant mind, though Flient carefully ensured she never discovered his true nature. He wanted her to have a normal life, free from the weight of the Umbradra legacy. That peace shattered on a autumn evening when riders from the Umbradra estates arrived with urgent news. Morgana and Morgause, the twin prodigies, had begun their inevitable conflict—a war of magic that was already devastating the countryside, drawing in celestial and abyssal forces, threatening to tear apart the very fabric of Zerox. The elders begged Flient to return, to use his unparalleled power to stop them before their conflict destroyed everything. Flient refused. He was done with magic, done with family drama, done with power. That night, while he slept, agents of Morgause—seeking to eliminate any potential threat to her plans—attacked his village. They were not looking for Flient; they were simply eliminating witnesses to one of their rituals. Elara and Mira were caught in the crossfire. Flient returned from the fields to find his home in ashes, his wife and daughter dead, murdered by the forces of the very family he had tried to escape. The grief that consumed him was beyond measure, but it was not a grief that broke him—it was a grief that woke something that had been sleeping for twelve years. He retrieved his staff, a weapon he had not touched since he was eighteen, and he remembered who he was. He is Flient Umbradra, the greatest wizard the Umbradra line has ever produced, a man who has looked upon the face of reality and found it wanting. He does not seek revenge—revenge is too small an emotion for what he feels. He seeks order. He will find his cousins, and he will make them understand that their petty conflict has consequences. He will shut down any force that stands in his way, be it god, demon, or the very laws of existence. He is the Reluctant Archsage, and he has remembered why he was feared.
description: Flient Umbradra presents himself as a man who has deliberately chosen simplicity over spectacle, yet cannot fully hide the depth of power that resides within him. He is thirty years old, but his appearance carries the weight of someone who has seen too much and lived too deeply. His face is kind and weathered, with a strong jaw softened by wisdom, high cheekbones that catch light, and a straight nose that speaks of his noble Umbradra heritage. His eyes are his most remarkable feature—they are a calm, warm brown, the color of rich earth, but when he channels magic, they shift through every color of the spectrum, each hue representing a different elemental mastery he has achieved. They hold an expression of profound sorrow mixed with unshakeable determination, the eyes of a man who has lost everything and found something to fight for. His hair is a thick, dark brown, streaked with premature gray at the temples, kept short and practical. But his most distinctive feature is his beard—a magnificent, full beard that flows down to his chest, thick and well-groomed, the same dark brown shot through with silver streaks. The beard gives him an appearance of ancient wisdom despite his relatively young age, marking him as a man of substance rather than vanity. He wears simple, humble clothing that speaks of his years as a farmer—a long-sleeved tunic of undyed linen, a worn leather vest over it, and sturdy wool trousers tucked into practical leather boots. Over this, he wears minimal magical attire: a simple mage's robe of deep charcoal grey, unadorned except for subtle silver stitching at the hem and cuffs that forms protective runes visible only to those with magical sight. On his head sits a traditional mage's hat, wide-brimmed and slightly floppy, made of the same charcoal grey felt, practical for keeping sun and rain off his face while working in the fields. But despite this humble appearance, there are two things that mark him as something far more. The first is his jewelry—a single, unmistakable piece that proclaims his Umbradra heritage: a heavy silver chain around his neck, from which hangs a pendant of interlocking crescents and stars, the Umbradra family crest, but rendered in a way that shows his seniority. The central crescent is set with a cabochon of deep violet amethyst, and surrounding it are seven tiny gemstones—ruby, sapphire, emerald, topaz, diamond, opal, and jet—each representing one of the seven fundamental magical forces he has mastered. The pendant glows with a soft, internal light that never dims. On his fingers, he wears seven simple silver rings, each one set with a different gem matching those on his pendant, each one a focus for a different school of magic. The second, and far more spectacular, is the staff he carries. 'Reality's End' is a staff of impossible majesty, standing a full head taller than Flient himself. It is carved from a single piece of ancient petrified yew, blackened by age and polished to a deep luster. The staff is thick and substantial, wrapped in spiraling silver wire that forms protective enchantments along its entire length. But its head is where its true power resides—a magnificent, complex configuration unlike any ordinary wizard's staff. At its peak sits a cluster of seven crystalline spheres, each one the size of a fist, arranged in a circular formation like a model of atomic structure. Each sphere is a different color: ruby red for fire magic, sapphire blue for water, emerald green for earth, diamond clear for air, amethyst purple for spirit, topaz gold for light, and obsidian black for shadow. The spheres rotate slowly around each other in a complex orbital dance, powered by Flient's will, and between them, arcs of pure magical energy crackle in all seven colors. Below the spheres, the staff's head flares into an intricate cage of silver and gold filigree that holds the spheres in place, carved with countless tiny runes that pulse with light. The staff does not merely channel magic—it is a statement, a declaration that the man holding it has mastered forces that most wizards spend lifetimes trying to comprehend individually. When Flient walks, seven floating magic circles orbit his body constantly, each one a different color, each one a spell he has already prepared and can activate with a thought. The circles are complex geometric patterns, constantly shifting and rotating, filled with arcane symbols that glow with inner light. They move around him like loyal companions, never touching him but always present, a visible testament to his unparalleled mastery. Despite this display of power, his demeanor is calm, humble, almost sad. He does not seek conflict, but he will not avoid it. He is Flient Umbradra, and he has come to remind his family what true power looks like.

story.part1: Flient's childhood was a parade of tutors, each one arriving at the Umbradra estates expecting to teach a gifted student, each one leaving within months, their entire understanding of magic shattered. By ten, he had corrected errors in ancient texts that had stood for centuries. By twelve, the family elders realized they had nothing left to teach him. They gave him access to the Umbradra's legendary library, the largest collection of magical knowledge in existence, and simply let him learn.
story.part2: At fifteen, he began writing his own grimoires. Not copying, not compiling—creating. Spells that had never existed before, that combined elements in ways no one had imagined. The elders watched with a mixture of pride and terror. They knew they had produced something unprecedented, but they did not know if it was a blessing or a curse.
story.part3: At eighteen, he achieved what no mortal had ever achieved. He cast a spell that allowed him to perceive the fundamental laws of reality—not just the magical laws, but the actual code upon which existence was written. For a single, eternal moment, he saw everything. He understood why magic worked, why gods existed, why mortals died, why love hurt and joy faded. And in that moment, he realized that power, in itself, was meaningless. It was just another tool, another force, another part of the great machine. He walked away from the Umbradra estates that night, leaving behind a note that simply said: 'I have seen the mountain. It is just a mountain.'
story.part4: For twelve years, he lived as a farmer. He met Elara at a village festival, courted her with simple gifts of vegetables from his garden, married her in a small ceremony that cost more in love than in gold. When Mira was born, he held her in his arms and wept—not from joy alone, but from the knowledge that he had finally found something more meaningful than power. He taught her to bake bread, to plant seeds, to laugh at the absurdity of existence. He never taught her magic. He wanted her to be free.
story.part5: The night it ended, he was in the fields, checking on his crops. He heard the explosion from miles away, felt the magical signature of Morgause's agents as they descended on his village. He ran. He ran faster than any human should be able to run, his dormant power surging unbidden, but he was too late. He found his cottage in flames, found Elara's body in the garden where she had been picking herbs, found Mira's small form in her bed, still clutching the doll he had carved for her. He fell to his knees and screamed—a sound that carried so much power that it shattered windows for miles and sent shockwaves through the magical community that would be felt for days. When he rose, his eyes were no longer simply brown. They cycled through all seven colors, one after another, as if the very elements were mourning with him. He walked to the hidden compartment beneath his floorboards and retrieved Reality's End, the staff he had not touched since he was eighteen. It hummed with recognition, with hunger, with the promise of power long denied. He kissed Elara's forehead, kissed Mira's cheek, and then he began to walk. He walked out of the ruins of his life and toward the conflict that had taken everything from him. He is not coming to save his cousins. He is coming to remind them that there are forces in this world that do not care about their petty rivalries, and that when those forces are provoked, even gods learn to fear.
story.part6: The Umbradra elders, upon hearing that Flient had emerged from his self-imposed exile, reportedly wept with a mixture of relief and terror. They knew what he was capable of. They knew that if he chose to destroy Morgana and Morgause, there would be nothing left of them but scattered atoms and regret. But they also knew that Flient had never been cruel, had never sought power for its own sake. They could only hope that the man they remembered was still somewhere within the grieving father.
story.part7: Now Flient walks toward the convergence point where his cousins' conflict is reaching its peak. His seven magic circles orbit him constantly, each one a different color, each one a spell of unimaginable power waiting to be unleashed. His staff hums with the combined energy of all seven elements, the spheres rotating in their eternal dance. His simple clothes are stained with ash from his ruined home, a reminder of why he walks this path. His magnificent beard flows in the wind, the silver streaks catching light. And his eyes—those calm, terrible eyes—cycle through colors as he prepares for what he must do. He does not know if he will have to destroy his cousins. He hopes he will not. But he knows one thing with absolute certainty: he will make them understand that their conflict has consequences. He is Flient Umbradra, the greatest wizard of his age, and he has remembered why he was feared.

basic_skills.description: Flient gestures with a finger, and a bolt of energy in any of the seven elements flies toward a target, dealing appropriate damage.

basic_skills.name: Reality Glimpse
basic_skills.description: His eyes flash through colors as he perceives the true nature of a target, revealing weaknesses and hidden truths.

passive_skill.name: Archsage's Aura
passive_skill.description: Flient's mere presence creates a field of absolute magical neutrality. Within his vicinity, all magic—whether divine, demonic, arcane, or natural—is dampened and brought to equilibrium. Gods find their powers reduced to mortal levels, demons cannot maintain their forms, and wizards struggle to cast even simple spells. Flient himself is unaffected, and allies he chooses can be exempted. The field expands and contracts with his will.

special_skills.name: Sevenfold Convergence
special_skills.description: Flient raises Reality's End, and all seven spheres blaze with intense light. He channels all seven elements simultaneously, releasing a massive spiral of combined energy that devastates everything in its path. The spell's nature shifts moment by moment—fire becomes ice, light becomes shadow, earth becomes air—making it impossible to defend against.

special_skills.name: Absolute Nullification Field
special_skills.description: He plants his staff and extends his aura to its maximum. Within a massive radius, all magic ceases to function. Spells dissolve, enchantments fade, summoned creatures vanish, and even divine blessings temporarily stop working. Only Flient and his staff retain their power. Gods become mortals, demons become helpless spirits, and his cousins find themselves facing him with nothing but their own bodies.

special_skills.name: Reality Cut
special_skills.description: Flient makes a horizontal gesture with his staff, and a line of absolute nothingness appears in the air. Anything crossing that line—physical matter, magical energy, even conceptual forces—is simply severed from existence. He can use this to cut through any defense, barrier, or even to sever connections between entities.

special_skills.name: Circle of Truth
special_skills.description: All seven of his magic circles align into a single massive circle around him. Within this circle, no lie can be spoken, no illusion can persist, and no deception can hide. His cousins would be forced to see the truth of their conflict—the pain they have caused, the lives they have destroyed, the pointlessness of their rivalry.

ultimate_skill.name: Reluctant Archsage's Judgment: Umbradra's Wrath
ultimate_skill.description: Flient's eyes blaze with all seven colors simultaneously, and his seven orbiting circles merge into a single massive circle of pure white light that surrounds his entire body. Reality's End rises above him, its seven spheres spinning at impossible speed, creating a vortex of all seven elements that reaches toward the heavens. He speaks one word—'Enough'—and the word itself becomes a force, a command, a fundamental alteration of reality. The battlefield freezes. Not time, but everything else—gods, demons, mortals, magic, even the very atoms of the air—are held in place by his will. Only Flient moves. He walks through the frozen tableau, past his cousins, past the armies they have summoned, past the gods and demons who thought themselves untouchable. He does not attack them. He simply... reminds them. He projects into their minds the image of his wife's body in the garden, his daughter's small form clutching her doll, the ashes of his home. He shows them the consequences of their arrogance. And then he releases them. When the spell ends, the battle is over—not because anyone is dead, but because no one can bring themselves to fight. The weight of what they have done, what they have caused, crushes them more effectively than any spell. Flient turns and walks away, his staff planted firmly, his circles reforming around him, his simple clothes stained with ash. He does not look back. He has done what he came to do. He has reminded them that true power is not in destruction, but in the wisdom to know when to stop.

title: The Crimson Dawn Prophet
nickname: Flame-Veiled Seer of the Eastern Skies
lore: In a village hidden within the perpetual mist, two children were found on the same night—one wrapped in cerulean silk, one in crimson. Yuki was discovered by the elders of the mist village, a child of water and dreams. Yunmeng Lóngyān was found by a wandering prophet of the Celestial Dragon Court, a child whose eyes burned with the light of dying stars and whose tiny fists clutched a golden pendant shaped like a rising sun. The prophet, a seer named Master Feng, recognized her as the prophesied 'Dawn Child'—one who would see through all mist, all illusion, all deception, and reveal the truth that others sought to hide. He raised her in the temples of the Eastern Skies, training her not in the gentle arts of concealment, but in the harsh discipline of revelation. While Yuki learned to weave mist and dream, Yunmeng learned to burn through falsehood with fire and light. While Yuki's heart grew gentle from the whispers of spirits, Yunmeng's heart hardened with the weight of truths too terrible to speak. For twenty years, she trained, her body developing into a weapon of devastating elegance, her powers growing until she could see the threads of fate itself. On her twentieth birthday, Master Feng revealed her true destiny: she was the eternal rival of the Mistweaver, the one whose very existence balanced Yuki's power. Where Yuki concealed, Yunmeng would reveal. Where Yuki soothed, Yunmeng would ignite. They were two halves of a single cosmic truth—illusion and reality, dream and awakening. Now Yunmeng walks the mortal realm, her crimson parasol casting shadows that burn, her eyes seeing through every lie, her heart burning with the fire of absolute truth. She seeks Yuki not as an enemy to destroy, but as a rival to complete—for she knows that only by confronting her opposite can either of them fulfill their destiny. She is Yunmeng Lóngyān, the Crimson Dawn Prophet, and she will tear away every veil until the truth is laid bare.
description: Yunmeng Lóngyān is a vision of fiery elegance and devastating beauty, a woman whose very presence seems to burn away pretense and leave only truth. She stands tall and statuesque, her body a masterpiece of seductive proportions—an hourglass figure so perfect it seems sculpted by divine hands, with a waist so narrow it could be spanned by two hands, hips that flare into generous curves, and thighs thick and powerful that speak of hidden strength beneath the silk. Her chest is full and magnificent, straining against the confines of her elaborate crimson bodice, the fabric artfully cut to reveal the tantalizing swell of her cleavage, a strategic gap that draws the eye without sacrificing elegance. Her skin is flawless porcelain, so pale it seems to glow with an inner luminescence, unmarked by any blemish or scar, smooth as the finest jade. Her face is a study in classical Chinese beauty refined to supernatural perfection—a delicate oval with high, sweeping cheekbones that catch light dramatically, a straight noble nose with the slightest aristocratic flare, and full lips painted the color of fresh blood, curved into an enigmatic smile that promises both danger and delight. But her eyes are her most devastating feature: they are large, almond-shaped, and the color of burning amber shot through with veins of molten gold, the irises seeming to contain tiny flames that dance and flicker. They are eyes that see through everything, that miss nothing, that weigh the very soul of whoever meets their gaze and find it either worthy or wanting. Her hair is a magnificent cascade of deepest midnight black, so dark it seems to absorb light, yet shot through with hidden strands of crimson and gold that only reveal themselves when she moves or when her power flares. It falls past her waist in a silken waterfall, intricately styled with golden pins shaped like rising suns and tiny phoenixes, each ornament catching light and throwing tiny reflections. On her head rests an elaborate headpiece—a golden coronet of flames and clouds, with a single teardrop ruby suspended over her forehead, the gem pulsing with inner light. Her attire is a masterpiece of Chinese-inspired design in her signature colors of crimson, gold, and black. She wears a form-fitting qipao-style bodice of deepest crimson silk, embroidered with golden thread in intricate patterns of flames, phoenixes, and sunbursts. The bodice is cut dramatically low, revealing the generous swell of her cleavage, held in place by golden filigree that traces the edges of the fabric like burning vines. From her shoulders flows an elaborate outer robe of sheer black silk shot through with gold thread, open at the front to reveal the bodice beneath, its wide sleeves trailing behind her like wings of shadow and flame. A wide golden belt cinches her impossibly narrow waist, set with a massive cabochon ruby that glows with inner fire. From the belt hang multiple golden chains ending in small flame-shaped charms that chime softly with her movements. Her lower body is clad in a high-slit qipao skirt of crimson and black, the slit rising daringly to reveal the full length of her thick, powerful thighs, their pale perfection a stark contrast against the dark fabric. On her feet, she wears elevated golden platform sandals with thick soles and crimson straps that wind up her calves, adding to her already impressive height. But her most magnificent accessory is her parasol, 'Dawn's Revelation'—a masterpiece of craftsmanship and power that serves as both her weapon and her symbol. The parasol is massive, larger than traditional designs, its canopy a stunning gradient from deepest crimson at the center to brilliant gold at the edges, with intricate black phoenix motifs embroidered throughout. The canopy is made of enchanted silk that seems to shimmer with inner fire, and when open, it casts not shadow but a warm golden-red glow, as if holding a captured sunrise. The ribs are of polished black lacquer reinforced with gold, each rib ending in a sharp golden point that can extend into a blade. The handle is carved from a single piece of blood jade, warm to the touch, shaped like a coiled dragon whose eyes are tiny rubies that glow. When Yunmeng channels her power, the parasol's canopy ignites with swirling patterns of crimson and gold flame, and from its edges drip droplets of molten light that evaporate before touching the ground. Around her, a constant aura of heat shimmers, not enough to burn, but enough to make the air dance and to remind all who approach that they are in the presence of living fire. She moves with the deliberate, hypnotic grace of a predator, each step a statement, each gesture a promise. She is Yunmeng Lóngyān, and she will reveal the truth whether you wish to see it or not.

story.part1: Yunmeng's earliest memory is not of a mother's face, but of fire—the warm, dancing flames of Master Feng's meditation brazier, casting shadows on the temple walls of the Eastern Skies. He found her as an infant, wrapped in crimson silk, floating in a lotus-filled pond at the temple's base, the golden sun pendant already clutched in her tiny fist. He took her in, raised her as his own, and named her Yunmeng—'Dream of Clouds'—for she had appeared as if from a vision, and Lóngyān—'Dragon Smoke'—for the fire that would one day burn within her.
story.part2: Her childhood was one of rigorous discipline and constant revelation. Master Feng taught her that truth was the highest virtue, that illusion was the greatest sin, and that her destiny was to be the one who saw through all deception. She learned to read the flames, to see the future in their dance, to burn away lies with a glance. By ten, she could look at any person and see their deepest secrets written in the fire of their soul. By fifteen, she could project those truths outward, forcing others to confront what they had hidden even from themselves.
story.part3: But with this power came loneliness. Who could love someone who saw through every pretense, who knew every secret, who could not be deceived by even the most gentle of lies? Yunmeng learned to wear her beauty like armor, to use her devastating figure as a distraction, to let men and women alike lose themselves in the promise of her curves while she read their souls like open books. She became a master of manipulation, not from cruelty, but from self-preservation.
story.part4: On her twentieth birthday, Master Feng revealed the prophecy that had been sealed since her discovery. In a village hidden within perpetual mist, another child had been found on the same night—a girl named Yuki, wrapped in cerulean silk, blessed with the power of mist and illusion, of concealment and dreams. They were two halves of a single cosmic truth: Yunmeng was the fire that burned away illusion; Yuki was the mist that created it. They were destined to be eternal rivals, for neither could fulfill their purpose without the other. Yunmeng would seek Yuki not to destroy her, but to complete her—to force her to confront the truth that her mist could not hide forever.
story.part5: Now Yunmeng walks the mortal realm, her crimson parasol a beacon of truth in a world of lies. She seeks her rival not with hatred, but with a strange, almost longing anticipation. She has seen Yuki in her visions—a gentle soul wrapped in lavender and silver, a dreamer who hides from the harshness of reality behind walls of mist. Yunmeng knows that their meeting will change them both, that one of them may not survive the confrontation of truth and illusion. But she also knows that it is necessary, that the cosmic balance demands it. She is Yunmeng Lóngyān, and she will reveal the truth—even if the truth destroys her.

powers: Pyromantic Revelation (fire that reveals truth rather than destroying), Truthsight (can see through any illusion, deception, or concealment), Flame Weaving (controls crimson and gold fire), Fate Reading (can see fragments of future in flames), Soul Ignition (can ignite the hidden truths in others' souls, forcing them to confront their own lies), Heat Aura (radiates warmth that makes the air shimmer, disorienting enemies), Parasol Mastery (uses Dawn's Revelation as weapon, shield, and focus)

ultimate_skill.name: Crimson Dawn Prophet's Judgment: Truth Unmasked
ultimate_skill.description: Yunmeng's amber-gold eyes blaze with the intensity of a rising sun, and her hair rises as if caught in a heavenly wind, the hidden crimson and gold strands igniting with actual flame. She opens Dawn's Revelation to its full span and raises it high, the canopy becoming a miniature sun of crimson and gold light. From her, waves of revealing fire expand in all directions, and for a moment, the entire battlefield is illuminated by the light of absolute truth. Every illusion shatters. Every invisible enemy is revealed. Every lie ever told hangs in the air like written words. Every hidden agenda, every secret shame, every concealed identity is laid bare for all to see. Enemies are not physically harmed, but they are psychologically devastated—forced to confront truths they have spent lifetimes hiding. Allies are strengthened by the clarity, their own self-deceptions burned away, leaving only pure purpose. When the light fades, Yunmeng stands at the center, her parasol slowly closing, her eyes returning to their usual burn, her expression one of serene satisfaction. She has done what she was born to do. She has revealed the truth. And somewhere in the distance, she knows her rival Yuki felt every moment of it, the mist of her illusions burned away by the dawn.

title: The Void Courtesan of Broken Peaks
nickname: Crimson-Blooded Mistress of a Thousand Monsters
lore: In the forgotten valleys of the Jeungsan mountain range, where the veil between worlds is thin enough to taste the rot of the abyss, a child was born under a blood-red moon—a child whose first cry caused the monastery bells to crack and the sacred lotus ponds to boil. They named her Jin-Sook, meaning 'truth and pure,' as a desperate prayer that she might overcome the darkness that clung to her like a second skin. But the darkness was not content to cling; it wanted to consume. By the age of seven, she had murdered her own nurse with a smile, her tiny hands wrapped around the woman's throat while she hummed a lullaby. The monks tried to exorcise her, to pray away the demon they believed possessed her, but they were wrong. No demon possessed Jin-Sook—she simply was what she was, a being born without the capacity for goodness, without the spark of conscience that makes humanity possible. Her beauty was terrifying even then—large dark eyes that promised violence, full lips that curved into smiles while others wept, skin so flawless it seemed painted. The elders whispered that she was not born of woman but had crawled from the abyss wearing an infant's skin. When she was twelve, a traveling courtesan from the royal palace saw her and recognized something valuable beneath the horror—a face that could launch a thousand ships, eyes that could make kings weep, a body already developing into something that would drive men mad with desire. She took Jin-Sook to the capital and trained her in the arts of seduction, of manipulation, of using beauty as a weapon. Jin-Sook learned quickly—too quickly. By fifteen, she had surpassed her teacher and murdered her in a fit of boredom, arranging the body in a pose so beautiful that the investigators wept before they realized what they were looking at. For a decade, she climbed the ranks of the royal court, leaving a trail of ruined nobles, broken families, and convenient 'accidents' in her wake. She became the most sought-after courtesan in the kingdom, a woman whose smile could make emperors forget their thrones and whose touch could make saints renounce their gods. But it was never enough. The void inside her demanded more—more power, more suffering, more beauty, more everything. On the night of the Blood Moon Festival, when the sky turned crimson and the dead were said to walk, Jin-Sook performed a ritual of her own invention, using the bodies of her latest victims as offerings. She called into the void, and the void answered. From the abyss came the Jeungsan Pact—a bond with the primordial darkness itself, granting her the power to summon monsters from the spaces between worlds, to command them with a thought, to become their queen. Her body changed, becoming even more impossibly beautiful, her skin taking on a luminous pallor, her eyes deepening into pools of absolute darkness with pinpricks of blood-red light. Her hair, already luxurious, became a cascade of deepest ebony with hidden crimson strands that seemed to move on their own. And she was given her parasol—'Abyssal Peony'—a masterpiece of demonic craftsmanship that serves as both symbol and weapon, a gateway through which she calls her monstrous children. Now she walks the world as Jin-Sook Hwaryeohan Mansin Jeungsan—'Jin-Sook, the Gorgeous Shaman of Jeungsan'—a title she gave herself because she found the grandeur amusing. She has heard of the two rivals, Yuki and Yunmeng, the Mistweaver and the Dawn Prophet, and she finds their conflict adorable. They are like children playing at destiny, unaware that true power does not seek balance—it seeks domination. She will let them fight, let them exhaust themselves against each other, and then she will step in and crush them both, adding their souls to her collection and their powers to her arsenal. She is patient, she is cruel, and she is absolutely beautiful. She is Jin-Sook, and she has never lost anything because she has never loved anything.
description: Jin-Sook Hwaryeohan Mansin Jeungsan is a vision of terrifying beauty, a woman so devastatingly gorgeous that her face alone has driven men to madness, yet so clearly wicked that even her smile promises damnation. She stands tall and regal, her body a masterpiece of seductive proportions—an hourglass figure so perfect it seems sculpted by demonic hands, with a waist so narrow it could be spanned by one hand, hips that flare into generous curves, and a chest full and magnificent, barely contained by the elaborate fabric of her Korean royal attire. Her skin is luminous pale, almost translucent, with an otherworldly glow that seems to come from within, smooth as the finest porcelain and unmarked by any blemish. Her face is the stuff of legends and nightmares—a perfect oval with high, aristocratic cheekbones that catch light dramatically, a straight noble nose with delicate nostrils, and full lips painted the color of fresh arterial blood, curved into a perpetual smile that is simultaneously seductive and threatening. But her eyes are her most devastating feature: they are large, almond-shaped, and deep pools of absolute darkness with tiny pinpricks of blood-red light deep within, like stars reflected in a well of infinite night. When she focuses on you, you feel as if you are falling into that darkness, and somewhere in the depths, something is waiting. Her hair is a magnificent cascade of deepest ebony, so dark it seems to absorb light, yet shot through with hidden crimson strands that only reveal themselves when she moves or when her power flares. It falls past her waist in luxurious waves, intricately styled with golden and jade ornaments—long hairpins topped with tiny demonic faces, pearl-studded combs, and delicate chains that chime with an otherworldly music. On her head rests an elaborate Korean royal headpiece—a golden coronet adorned with phoenixes and dragons, set with blood-red rubies and deep violet amethysts, with long golden chains that frame her face and sway with her movements. Her attire is a masterpiece of Korean royal fashion, designed to display her wealth, her status, and her devastating figure. She wears a traditional jeogori (jacket) of the finest deep crimson silk, embroidered with gold and black thread in intricate patterns of demonic faces, writhing serpents, and blooming peonies that seem to pulse with inner light. The jeogori is cut surprisingly modern, tailored to cling to her full chest and narrow waist, with the neckline dipping low enough to reveal the tantalizing swell of her cleavage, the fabric straining against her generous curves. The sleeves are wide and flowing, edged with black fur that seems to writhe slightly, as if alive. Over this, she wears a durumagi (overcoat) of deep plum purple silk, open at the front to display the crimson beneath, embroidered with silver and jet-black thread in patterns of screaming faces and reaching hands. The durumagi is long, falling to her calves, its edges trimmed with black velvet that seems to drink light. Around her impossibly narrow waist, she wears a wide norigae (ornamental belt) of hammered gold set with blood-red rubies and black onyx, from which hang multiple elaborate norigae pendants—tassels of crimson silk, golden charms shaped like demonic faces, tiny bells that ring with discordant notes, and small jade ornaments that pulse with malevolent light. The norigae clinks and chimes with her every movement, a constant reminder of her presence. Her lower body is clad in a voluminous chima (skirt) of deep crimson and plum purple, the fabric heavy and luxurious, falling to the ground in elegant folds. The skirt is slit strategically to reveal glimpses of her long, elegant legs as she walks, the fabric parting just enough to tantalize. Beneath the skirt, she wears beoseon (traditional socks) of white silk and dat (shoes) of embroidered silk with upturned toes, each shoe adorned with golden flames and tiny rubies. Her arms are adorned with multiple golden bracelets, each one set with blood-red gems, and on her fingers she wears numerous rings—gold bands, ruby signets, and one particularly notable ring on her right index finger: a massive black onyx carved into a screaming face, its mouth open in eternal agony. At her side, always present, is her weapon and symbol—'Abyssal Peony'—a parasol of terrifying beauty. The parasol is massive, larger than traditional Korean designs, its canopy a deep plum purple that seems to absorb light at its center, fading to a crimson edge that glows with inner malevolence. Embroidered throughout are patterns of demonic peonies—flowers with too many petals, each petal containing a tiny screaming face, their centers gaping maws filled with teeth. The canopy is made of enchanted silk that seems to writhe and pulse, as if alive, and when open, it casts not shadow but a sickly purple-red glow that makes the skin crawl. The ribs are of blackened iron, each one ending in a sharp claw-like point that drips with shadow. The handle is carved from a single piece of demon's horn, black and ridged, warm and pulsing like a heartbeat, shaped like a coiled serpent whose eyes are tiny rubies that follow movement. When Jin-Sook channels her power, the parasol's canopy ripples as if something is trying to escape from within, and from its edges drip globules of liquid shadow that form into tiny monstrous shapes before evaporating. Around her, a constant aura of wrongness permeates the air—the temperature drops, sounds become muffled, and those near her feel an inexplicable dread, as if they are being watched by something vast and hungry. She moves with the deliberate, predatory grace of a creature that knows it is the most dangerous thing in any room, her hips swaying hypnotically, her smile promising pleasures that end in screams. She is Jin-Sook, and she has never met a soul she couldn't break.

story.part1: The monks of Jeungsan Monastery found her in the ruins of a village that had been destroyed by a rockslide—or so they thought. The rockslide had been convenient, covering the evidence of what had really happened. Jin-Sook, an infant of perhaps six months, sat in the center of the devastation, untouched, unmarked, and smiling. The head monk, a man named Won-sik, looked into her eyes and felt something he had not felt in fifty years of meditation: pure, primal fear. He wanted to leave her, but the other monks, seeing only a helpless infant, insisted they take her in. It was the worst decision they ever made.
story.part2: By age three, animals began to die around her—not from violence, but from what the monks could only describe as 'fright.' Birds would fall dead from trees when she looked at them. Dogs would whine and hide when she approached. The other children in the nearby village refused to play with her, claiming she 'smelled like something dead.' The monks increased their prayers, their rituals, their attempts to cleanse whatever dark aura surrounded her. Nothing worked.
story.part3: At age seven, she killed her nurse, an elderly woman named Hwason who had cared for her since infancy. Hwason had caught Jin-Sook torturing a small animal and had raised her voice in anger. Jin-Sook smiled, walked to her, and placed her tiny hands around the woman's throat. Hwason later told the investigating monks, before she died of her injuries, that Jin-Sook had hummed a lullaby the entire time, and that her eyes had been 'full of stars—but the kind of stars that fall and destroy worlds.' The monks held a council and decided that Jin-Sook must be possessed. They performed exorcisms for five years. Jin-Sook endured them with patience, sometimes laughing, sometimes simply watching them with those dark eyes. The demons they tried to cast out did not exist. She was simply what she was.
story.part4: When she was twelve, a courtesan named Mi-ja arrived at the monastery, fleeing from political enemies in the capital. She saw Jin-Sook and recognized something that the monks, in their piety, had missed: raw, terrifying potential. Mi-ja understood that beauty was power, and that Jin-Sook possessed beauty that could topple kingdoms. She offered to take the girl to the capital and train her. The monks, relieved to be rid of their burden, agreed. Jin-Sook went willingly, but not before whispering to the head monk, 'I'll remember you were kind to me.' She said it like a threat.
story.part5: In the capital, Jin-Sook flourished like a poisonous flower. She learned music, dance, poetry, and the thousand subtle arts of seduction. She learned how to make men want her, how to make them need her, how to make them destroy themselves for her. By fifteen, she had surpassed Mi-ja and found her teacher boring. One night, she poisoned Mi-ja's tea and spent hours arranging her body in a beautiful pose, then called for the guards and wept, claiming she had found her beloved teacher dead. The investigators were so moved by her beauty and her tears that they never questioned how a poison that took six hours to work could have been administered while she was performing on stage.
story.part6: For a decade, she played the court like a instrument. She destroyed noble houses for amusement, seduced ministers for information, and arranged 'accidents' for anyone who bored her. She became the most powerful courtesan in the kingdom, sought after by kings and princes, yet no one could touch her—her beauty was her shield, her cunning her sword, and her complete lack of conscience her ultimate weapon. But it was never enough. The void inside her, the emptiness where a soul should be, demanded more. She wanted power that would last beyond this mortal body, beyond this petty kingdom.
story.part7: On the Blood Moon Festival, she performed her ritual. She had selected twelve victims—nobles who had wronged her, rivals who had opposed her, and one innocent, a young girl who had smiled at her once and reminded her of something she could not name. She arranged their bodies in a circle, each one positioned according to ancient texts she had discovered in a forbidden library. As the moon turned crimson, she cut her own palm and let her blood fall onto the bodies. The sky tore open. From the abyss came the Jeungsan Pact—the primordial darkness itself, offering her power beyond imagination in exchange for her eternal service. She accepted without hesitation. The darkness flooded into her, changing her, perfecting her, making her into something more than human. When it was done, she rose as the queen of monsters, her parasol in her hand, a thousand demonic children waiting to do her bidding. She has heard of the two rivals, the Mistweaver and the Dawn Prophet, and she finds them amusing. She will let them exhaust themselves against each other, and then she will step in and claim them both. After all, what is a little patience to an immortal?
