She can then use this stolen identity to infiltrate, deceive, or destroy.

special_skills.name: Memory Rewrite
special_skills.description: Deigeini touches the Silver-Tongued Dagger to a target's forehead and whispers a new memory. The target's mind rewrites itself, inserting the fabricated memory as if it had always been there. A hero becomes a traitor, a lover becomes a stranger, a lifetime of trust becomes a moment of betrayal.

ultimate_skill.name: Deceit's Judgment: The Eternal Lie
ultimate_skill.description: Deigeini Moratta's silver eyes blaze with the light of a thousand false dawns, and her four magnificent moth wings spread to their full span, each wing now twenty feet across, their patterns shifting and swirling with faces and lies and desperate truths. She raises the Mirror of False Truths high above her head, and the mirror expands, growing to immense size, its surface becoming a swirling vortex of silver light. She speaks a single, silken word: 'Believe.' In that moment, the battlefield becomes a lie. Every enemy is caught in the mirror's gaze, and they see not reality but the most beautiful lie they could ever imagine—their greatest victory, their loved one returned, their deepest desire fulfilled, all rendered in perfect, heartbreaking detail. They believe it completely. They laugh, they cry, they reach out to embrace phantoms. While they are lost in their beautiful lies, Deigeini moves among them on silent feet, her hips swaying, her wings rustling softly. With the Silver-Tongued Dagger, she makes a single, delicate cut on each one, not to kill, but to seal the lie forever. They will live the rest of their existence in that perfect fantasy, never knowing it's false, never wanting to know. When the vision fades, the enemies are still standing, but their eyes are empty, their faces frozen in expressions of eternal bliss, trapped in dreams that will never end. Deigeini stands at the center, the Mirror of False Truths now returned to its normal size, held against her chest. She looks at the smiling, empty shells around her and smiles her knowing smile. They are happy. That is the greatest lie of all. She is Deigeini Moratta. She is Deceit. And you can believe anything she tells you.

title: Betrayal • The Crimson Fox
lore: In the ancient forests of Hokkaido, Japan, there lived a woman named Feinkuri Futaka who was known for her unwavering loyalty. She was a shrine keeper, the last in a long line of priestesses who tended to a small, forgotten shrine deep in the woods. Her family had served the shrine's fox spirit for seventeen generations, and Feinkuri took her duty seriously—more seriously than anything else in her life. She lived alone, devoted entirely to the shrine, to the spirit she called 'Kitsune-sama.' She spoke to it daily, left offerings, kept the grounds immaculate. In return, she felt its presence, a warm, protective energy that was the only family she had ever known. When she was twenty-three, developers came to the forest. They wanted to build a resort, to cut down the ancient trees, to destroy the shrine. Feinkuri fought them with every tool she had—protests, petitions, even physical confrontation. But they had money and power, and she had only her faith. One night, the lead developer, a man named Tanaka, came to the shrine alone. He offered her a deal: if she would renounce her spirit, declare it false, and help them demolish the shrine, they would pay her enough money to live comfortably for the rest of her life. She refused. He smiled and showed her photographs—her shrine, her sacred space, already half-destroyed. They had started without permission, and by the time the courts acted, it would be too late. clothing: Kurikurimiji wears a form-fitting battle dress of deep violet silk and silver chainmail, the fabric cut to accentuate every curve of her hourglass figure while allowing maximum mobility. The bodice is low-cut, revealing the generous swell of her breasts, with silver chainmail panels that offer protection without concealing. The dress is slit strategically on the sides to allow for unrestricted movement, exposing glimpses of her long perfect legs and thick thighs. A wide belt of woven silver chains cinches her impossibly small waist, from which hang small silver pouches containing preserved specimens of suffering. Silver armlets in the shape of mantis claws adorn her upper arms, and matching greaves protect her shins.
accessories: Small silver teardrop earrings; a stunning silver and violet gemstone necklace with a large teardrop violet sapphire resting in her cleavage; the woven silver chain belt with small pouches; mantis claw-shaped silver armlets and greaves; several silver rings with violet gems; small mantis claw pins in her hair; soft violet leather boots.

weapon.name: Smiling Edge
weapon.aura: The scythe glows with a soft, violet light, and those near it feel a strange calm, as if their suffering has already been accepted, already been appreciated. The air around it shimmers with heat distortion and the faint sound of distant screams.
weapon.special_feature: The Smiling Edge is a massive, curved scythe forged from the same otherworldly violet chitin as Kurikurimiji's natural blades, its handle wrapped in pale leather that is actually preserved human skin—donated by particularly beautiful specimens. The blade is nearly five feet long, curving in an elegant arc, its edge impossibly sharp and gleaming with inner violet light. The scythe is not just a weapon; it is an artist's tool, designed to harvest suffering with surgical precision. Each swing is a study in angles and pressure, designed to cause maximum pain with minimum waste. Wounds inflicted by the Smiling Edge bleed not just blood but also the victim's emotional pain, which Kurikurimiji can then collect. The scythe can also be used to 'cut' emotional bonds to happiness, leaving victims in a state of perpetual melancholy.
special_skills: Harvest Swing (a precise cut that extracts emotional pain along with blood)
Smiling Arc (a sweeping strike that causes multiple wounds, each one a study in suffering)
Joy Sever (a cut that severs the victim's capacity for happiness)
Specimen Collection (wounds created by the scythe are 'preserved' for later study)

weapon.name: Specimen's Lament
weapon.aura: The cage glows with a soft, violet light, and within it, tiny specks of colored light swirl and dance—each one a captured scream, a preserved tear, a final moment. Those near it hear faint whispers of suffering.
weapon.special_feature: The Specimen's Lament is a delicate, ornate cage of twisted silver and violet crystal, small enough to hold in one hand but containing multitudes. The cage is hexagonal, each side a different panel of crystal that pulses with inner light, and within it, Kurikurimiji stores her collections—screams rendered as tiny wisps of colored light, tears preserved as perfect crystal droplets, final words as shimmering script that writes itself on the air. The cage allows her to relive any collected moment of suffering, studying it from every angle, appreciating its unique beauty. She can also release these collected sufferings as weapons—unleashing a captured scream to terrify enemies, or a preserved tear to flood them with melancholy. The cage is her gallery, her laboratory, her greatest treasure.
special_skills: Scream Release (unleashes a captured scream that terrifies enemies)
Tear Flood (releases preserved tears that flood victims with sadness)
Final Word (speaks a victim's last words, causing psychological damage)
Specimen Study (enters a trance to study collected suffering, gaining power from each memory)

basic_skills.name: Violet Gaze
basic_skills.description: Kurikurimiji fixes her pupil-less violet eyes on a target. The target feels suddenly, inexplicably studied, as if they are under a microscope, every weakness catalogued, every vulnerability noted. They become hyper-aware of their own pain, past and present.

basic_skills.name: Mantis Strike
basic_skills.description: Her shoulder blades flash forward in a blindingly fast strike, the curved chitin slicing through armor and flesh before the target even registers movement. The cut is precise, artistic, and leaves a wound that throbs with remembered pain.

basic_skills.name: Wing Burst
basic_skills.description: Her delicate mantis wings flare open and she vanishes in a blur of violet light, reappearing instantly behind a target, her smile unchanged, her blades already moving.

passive_skill.name: Aura of Detached Curiosity
passive_skill.description: Kurikurimiji radiates an aura of profound, unsettling calm at all times. All within range feel as if they are being studied, observed, catalogued—not with malice, but with the detached curiosity of a scientist examining specimens. This aura makes enemies hyper-aware of their own vulnerabilities, causing them to flinch, hesitate, and second-guess every move. The longer someone remains in her presence, the more they feel like an insect pinned to a board, waiting to be examined.

special_skills.name: Gallery of Suffering
special_skills.description: Kurikurimiji raises the Specimen's Lament and opens its crystal panels. From within, hundreds of captured screams, preserved tears, and final moments pour forth, filling the battlefield with a symphony of suffering. Enemies are overwhelmed by the collective agony of countless victims, their minds flooded with pain not their own, leaving them paralyzed and weeping.

special_skills.name: Artful Harvest
special_skills.description: She swings the Smiling Edge in a series of precise, almost dance-like movements, each cut a deliberate study in pain. She does not kill quickly—she kills artistically, each wound placed to cause maximum suffering, each scream a note in her composition. By the end, her enemies are masterpieces of agony.

special_skills.name: Specimen Study
special_skills.description: Kurikurimiji fixes her violet eyes on a single target and enters a trance-like state. For several moments, she simply watches them—their movements, their expressions, their fear. During this time, she learns every vulnerability, every weakness, every secret source of pain. When she finally moves, her attacks are perfectly calibrated to cause the maximum possible suffering.

ultimate_skill.name: Cruelty's Judgment: The Eternal Exhibition
ultimate_skill.description: Kurikurimiji Muji's violet eyes blaze with inner light, and her four mantis blades extend to their full length, gleaming with malevolent radiance. Her delicate wings spread wide, vibrating at a frequency that produces a soft, almost beautiful hum. She raises the Smiling Edge high above her head and opens the Specimen's Lament with a gesture, its crystal panels swinging wide. She speaks a single, curious word: 'Observe.' In that moment, the battlefield transforms into her personal gallery. Every enemy is frozen in place, not by magic, but by the sudden, overwhelming sensation of being studied. They feel Kurikurimiji's gaze on each of them, patient, curious, eternal. Then the exhibition begins. From the Specimen's Lament, every collected moment of suffering pours forth—screams become visible as waves of colored light, tears as crystalline rain, final moments as living dioramas that play out before each victim's eyes. The enemies are forced to witness suffering, to experience it vicariously, to understand it in ways they never imagined. While they are lost in the exhibition, Kurikurimiji moves among them with her Smiling Edge, her movements slow and deliberate, each cut a new addition to her collection. She does not kill them—that would be wasteful. Instead, she harvests their screams, preserves their tears, captures their final moments, adding them to her eternal gallery. When the exhibition ends, the enemies are still standing, but they are empty—their capacity for suffering has been extracted, preserved, and displayed. They feel nothing now, not even relief. Kurikurimiji stands at the center, the Specimen's Lament full of new treasures, the Smiling Edge gleaming with fresh light. She smiles her gentle, curious smile. She is Kurikurimiji Muji. She is Cruelty. And the exhibition is always open.

title: Cowardice • The Shadow Hare
lore: In the war-torn villages of feudal Korea, there lived a man named Zorgbein Fikas who was born with a heart that beat too fast. From his earliest memories, he was afraid—of the dark, of strangers, of the soldiers who occasionally passed through, of his own shadow. His father, a veteran of countless battles, tried to beat the fear out of him. His mother prayed to every spirit she knew. Nothing worked. Zorgbein was simply, fundamentally, irredeemably afraid. When the Japanese invasions came, his village was caught between armies. While other young men took up rusty swords and farming tools to defend their homes, Zorgbein ran. He ran into the mountains and hid in a cave, listening to the screams drift up from below, trembling with fear and shame. He stayed there for three days, too terrified to move, too terrified to even eat. When he finally crept back down, his village was ash. Everyone he had ever known was dead—his father with a sword in his hand, his mother with her prayer beads still clutched in her fingers. The other survivors, those who had fought and lived, looked at him with contempt. 'Where were you, coward?' they asked. He had no answer. For years afterward, Zorgbein tried to prove himself. He joined a resistance group, determined to fight, to die if necessary, to redeem himself. But every time battle approached, his body betrayed him. His heart would race, his hands would shake, his legs would carry him away before his mind could stop them. He would find himself hiding, trembling, while others died. He became a joke, a cautionary tale, the man who ran. One night, his group was ambushed. His comrades fought and died around him, and once again, Zorgbein ran. He ran until his legs gave out, collapsed in a forest, and wept. He wept for his village, for his parents, for his comrades, for himself. And as he wept, he realized the truth: he would always run. It was not a choice. It was what he was. Vergasuis appeared then, leaning against a tree with those dying-star eyes gleaming in the darkness. 'You think cowardice is weakness,' the demon king said. 'But I have watched you for years. You are not weak. You are simply... optimized for survival. You have a gift that others lack—the ability to know when to flee, to live when others die. Most call it cowardice. I call it wisdom.' He offered Zorgbein a deal: become Cowardice itself, a being who could run faster than any threat, who could hide where none could find, who would never have to feel that shame again because running would be his purpose, his power, his art. Zorgbein accepted. His body transformed in a blur of shadow and silver. His legs elongated, becoming powerful and spring-loaded, built for impossible speed. His eyes grew large and luminous, deep silver with vertical pupils, capable of seeing threats from miles away, of perceiving the fastest escape route in an instant. From the top of his head, two enormous hare ears emerged—sensitive, twitching, able to hear a heartbeat from a league away. His skin took on a pale, silvery-grey luminescence, smooth as moonlight. His hair became a cascade of silver-white, shot through with streaks of deep shadow-grey. From his lower back, a short, fluffy hare tail emerged—small, almost comical, but twitching constantly with awareness. But his face remained human—more handsome than ever, with high Korean cheekbones, full lips, and eyes that now held not fear but eternal, watchful awareness. He rose from that forest and found the soldiers who had killed his comrades. He did not fight them. He ran past them, faster than they could see, and as he passed, he whispered in each ear: 'Run.' They felt his fear, his cowardice, transmitted like a virus, and suddenly they were running too, away from nothing, away from everything, their courage shattered. Zorgbein watched them flee and felt not shame but satisfaction. He had survived. He always survived. Now, Zorgbein rules his domain, an endless labyrinth of shadow and light where paths shift constantly, where hiding places are infinite, where the only rule is survival. He is Zorgbein Fikas, and he will never stop running—because running is what he does best.
description: Zorgbein Fikas is cowardice made manifest, a being of such ethereal beauty that you almost don't notice he's already gone. He stands at a lithe six feet one inch, his form lean and aerodynamic, every muscle designed for one purpose: speed. His body is a vision of masculine perfection—broad shoulders tapering to a narrow waist, a perfectly defined chest with visible abs, powerful arms with corded muscle, and most strikingly, his legs: impossibly long and powerful, built like a sprinter's, thick thighs that could launch him across continents, and elegant calves that seem to never tire. His skin is pale silvery-grey with a subtle luminescence, smooth as moonlight and flawless as untouched snow, cool to the touch like shadows given form. His face is breathtakingly handsome in a classical Korean way—high prominent cheekbones that catch the light, a straight nose with refined bridge, full lips that are usually curved in a slight, knowing smile that speaks not of fear but of eternal vigilance, and a strong, determined jawline. But his eyes are his most striking feature: they are large, luminous pools of deep silver with vertical slit pupils, holding an eternal, watchful awareness that misses nothing, that constantly scans for threats, that has already calculated seventeen escape routes before you've finished your first sentence. When he looks at you, you feel not threatened but observed—as if he's already decided whether you're a threat worth fleeing from. His most distinctive features are his ears and tail. From the top of his head, two enormous hare ears emerge from his silver-white hair—each ear nearly two feet long, covered in soft silvery-grey fur with white tips, incredibly sensitive, constantly twitching and rotating like radar dishes, picking up every sound for miles. They can hear a heartbeat from a league away, a whisper from across a battlefield, the slightest shift in the wind that might signal danger. From his lower back, just above his hips, a small, fluffy hare tail emerges—round and soft, covered in the same silvery-grey fur with a white tip, constantly twitching with awareness, almost comically small compared to his ears but just as sensitive to his surroundings. His hair is a magnificent cascade of silver-white, long and flowing, with streaks of deep shadow-grey that seem to absorb light, falling past his shoulders in soft waves, often adorned with small silver rings that catch the light as he moves. His attire is a masterpiece of functional elegance. He wears a form-fitting bodysuit of deep grey and silver fabric that seems to shift color with his movement, blending into shadows and light alike. The fabric is lightweight and silent, allowing him to move without a sound, and is strategically cut to reveal his muscular physique—the V-shaped torso visible through the open chest panel, the defined abs on display, the powerful arms bare from shoulder to wrist. Over this, he wears a short haori-style jacket of deep charcoal grey, embroidered with silver thread in patterns of running hares and shifting shadows, the jacket open and flowing, designed to catch the wind and add to his speed. A wide belt of woven silver cords cinches his narrow waist, from which hang small pouches containing escape routes he has memorized and threats he has catalogued. Silver armlets in the shape of running hares adorn his upper arms, and matching anklets circle his powerful ankles. Around his neck, he wears a simple but elegant necklace of silver and shadow-grey gems, with a single, large teardrop silver sapphire resting at the hollow of his throat. On his fingers, he wears several silver rings, each set with a shadow-grey gem that pulses with inner light when danger is near. On his feet, he wears soft boots of deep grey leather, soled for silence and designed for maximum speed, the boots extending to just below his knees. In his elegant hands, he carries his legendary weapons: the Fleeting Shadow and the Heartstart Bow. The Fleeting Shadow is a pair of wickedly curved daggers, forged from shadow-stuff and silver, their blades semi-transparent and almost invisible in motion, designed for quick strikes as he passes—hit-and-run tactics elevated to art form. The Heartstart Bow is an elegant, recurve bow carved from pale wood that seems to grow from shadow, its string made of woven moonlight, and its arrows are not physical but manifestations of fear—when they strike, they inject pure terror into the victim, making them feel what Zorgbein once felt: the overwhelming, paralyzing need to run. He moves with impossible speed, a blur of silver and shadow, here one moment and gone the next, his ears always twitching, his eyes always scanning, his body always ready to flee. He is Zorgbein Fikas, and he will outrun anything.

story.part1: Zorgbein's earliest memories are of fear. Not the rational fear of a child, but a deep, existential terror that clung to everything. He was afraid of his father's belt, of the soldiers at the gates, of the dark, of the light, of himself. He could not explain it; he could only feel it.
story.part2: His father tried to beat the fear out of him. It didn't work. His mother prayed for him. It didn't work. The village shaman performed rituals. Nothing worked. Zorgbein was simply, fundamentally afraid, and nothing could change that.
story.part3: When the invasion came, he ran. He ran into the mountains and hid while his village burned. He heard the screams of his parents, his neighbors, his friends, and he trembled in his cave, too terrified to move. When he returned, they were all dead.
story.part4: The survivors looked at him with contempt. 'Coward,' they called him. He tried to prove them wrong, joining the resistance, forcing himself to fight. But every time battle approached, his body betrayed him. He ran. He always ran.
story.part5: The night his comrades were ambushed, he ran again. He ran until he collapsed, and then he wept. He wept for them, for himself, for the shame that would never leave him. And in that moment of absolute despair, he accepted what he was.
story.part6: Vergasuis appeared and offered him a different perspective: his cowardice was not weakness but survival instinct perfected. The demon king offered him the power to run forever, to never be caught, to never feel shame again. Zorgbein accepted.
story.part7: Now, Zorgbein rules his domain, an endless labyrinth where he is always one step ahead, always just out of reach. He watches threats approach and smiles, because he knows something they don't: he can always run faster. He is Zorgbein Fikas, and he has finally found peace—in motion, in flight, in the eternal act of running away.

powers: Fear Sense (can sense fear, danger, and threat from miles away, perceiving the exact nature and location of any potential harm), Hyper-Speed (can move at impossible speeds, appearing as a blur of silver and shadow, outrunning almost anything), Threat Calculation (his mind constantly calculates escape routes, danger levels, and survival probabilities with superhuman accuracy), Ear Sensitivity (his enormous hare ears can hear heartbeats from a league away, whispers from across battlefields, and the slightest shift in wind that might signal danger), Fear Injection (his touch, his weapons, and even his presence can inject pure terror into others, making them feel the overwhelming need to flee), Shadow Blending (his body can blend into shadows and light, becoming nearly invisible when he holds still), Dagger Mastery (wields the Fleeting Shadow daggers with hit-and-run precision), Bow Mastery (wields the Heartstart Bow to inject fear from a distance)
speciality: Escape, Evasion, Fear Manipulation, Hit-and-Run Tactics

weapon.name: Fleeting Shadow
weapon.aura: The daggers are semi-transparent, almost invisible in motion, leaving trails of shadow and silver light. Those near them feel a sudden urge to run, to flee, to escape.
weapon.special_feature: The Fleeting Shadow is a pair of wickedly curved daggers, forged from shadow-stuff and silver, their blades semi-transparent and almost impossible to track when in motion. Each dagger is about eighteen inches long, curving gracefully like a hare's leap, with edges so sharp they cut through air without a sound. The hilts are wrapped in pale grey leather and capped with silver hares in mid-run. The daggers are designed for hit-and-run tactics—quick strikes as Zorgbein passes, leaving wounds that bleed not just blood but courage. A single cut from these daggers makes the victim feel the overwhelming need to run, to flee, to escape, even if there's no danger. They become infected with cowardice, their bravery draining away with every heartbeat.
special_skills: Passing Strike (a quick cut as Zorgbein runs past, injecting fear)
Shadow Throw (throws the dagger, which becomes almost invisible in flight)
Courage Drain (wounds bleed bravery, leaving victims fearful)
Escape Cut (a precise strike that makes the victim run from nothing)

weapon.name: Heartstart Bow
weapon.aura: The bow glows with a soft silver light, and those aimed at feel their hearts race, their palms sweat, their breath quicken—the first signs of fear. The arrows it fires are invisible, visible only as trails of silver terror.
weapon.special_feature: The Heartstart Bow is an elegant, recurve bow carved from pale wood that seems to grow from shadow itself, its surface smooth and cool, etched with images of running hares and fleeing figures. The string is made of woven moonlight, nearly invisible but impossibly strong. The bow does not fire physical arrows; instead, it fires manifestations of pure fear, drawn from Zorgbein's eternal well of terror and shaped into projectiles by his will. When one of these fear-arrows strikes a target, it does no physical damage but injects pure, overwhelming terror directly into their soul. They experience what Zorgbein once experienced—the paralyzing, all-consuming need to run, to flee, to escape. Strong-willed targets may resist, but even they will find their courage shaken, their hands trembling, their resolve wavering.
special_skills: Terror Shot (injects pure fear into the target, making them flee)
Panic Volley (fires multiple fear-arrows, creating chaos and flight)
Heartstopper (a precision shot that targets the victim's courage directly)
Running Blind (arrows that make victims run without knowing why)

basic_skills.name: Silver Gaze
basic_skills.description: Zorgbein fixes his luminous silver eyes on a target. The target feels suddenly, inexplicably afraid—not of him, but of everything. Their heart races, their palms sweat, and they feel an overwhelming urge to look over their shoulder, to run, to hide.

basic_skills.name: Ear Twitch
basic_skills.description: His enormous hare ears twitch and rotate, picking up every sound within miles. He can hear a target's heartbeat, their breathing, their whispered plans, and knows exactly where they are and what they're feeling.

basic_skills.name: Blur Strike
basic_skills.description: Zorgbein vanishes in a blur of silver and shadow, reappearing behind a target for the briefest moment—just long enough to leave a shallow cut from his Fleeting Shadow daggers before vanishing again, already gone, already running.

passive_skill.name: Aura of Flight
passive_skill.description: Zorgbein radiates an aura of perpetual motion and escape at all times. All within range feel an inexplicable urge to run, to flee, to escape—not from anything specific, just from everything. This aura makes enemies jittery, unfocused, and prone to panicking. Their courage slowly drains away the longer they remain near him, replaced by the same eternal fear that drives him. Allies, oddly, feel motivated to keep moving, to not give up, to run toward their goals rather than away.

special_skills.name: Garden of Flight
special_skills.description: Zorgbein draws his Heartstart Bow and fires a single arrow into the sky. It explodes into a rain of silver light, and when the light touches the ground, the battlefield transforms into an endless plain with no cover, no hiding places, nowhere to run—except that everywhere is the perfect direction to run. Enemies become disoriented, unsure where safety lies, and many simply start running in random directions, unable to stop.

special_skills.name: Eternal Escape
special_skills.description: Zorgbein begins to run, and as he runs, he leaves behind trails of silver light that form into afterimages of himself—dozens of them, hundreds, all running in different directions. Enemies don't know which one is real, which way he's going, where to strike. Meanwhile, the real Zorgbein circles back, his daggers ready, his bow drawn.

special_skills.name: Fear Inheritance
special_skills.description: Zorgbein focuses on a target and, with his silver eyes, shows them his memories—every moment of terror, every time he ran, every shame-filled flight. The target experiences his lifetime of fear in an instant, and unless they have an iron will, they break, their own courage replaced by his accumulated cowardice.

ultimate_skill.name: Cowardice's Judgment: The Flight That Never Ends
ultimate_skill.description: Zorgbein Fikas's silver eyes blaze with the light of a thousand panicked moments, and his enormous hare ears spread wide, catching every sound within the cosmos. He draws the Heartstart Bow to its full extension, and from the string, not one arrow but a thousand manifest—each one a lifetime of fear, each one targeting a different enemy. He speaks a single, whispered word: 'Run.' In that moment, he releases. The thousand fear-arrows fly in every direction, each one seeking its target with impossible precision. When they strike, they do not wound flesh; they wound the soul. Every enemy on the battlefield is suddenly flooded with the absolute, overwhelming terror that Zorgbein has felt his entire existence. They experience every moment of his cowardice, every shameful flight, every pounding heart, every trembling hand. And then they feel something worse: they feel his acceptance. They understand that running is not weakness—it is survival. It is wisdom. It is the only honest response to a world that wants to kill you. And so they run. They drop their weapons and run, not from anything specific, but from everything. They run until their legs give out, and then they crawl, still running, still fleeing, still trying to escape a danger that exists only in their now-terrified minds. Zorgbein watches them go, his expression calm, his ears twitching, his body still. He does not pursue. He does not need to. They are doing what he does best. They are running. He is Zorgbein Fikas. He is Cowardice. And he has finally found the courage to be afraid.

title: Ignorance • The Blind Owl
nickname: He Who Sees Nothing and Knows Everything
lore: In the ancient libraries of the Mongol Empire, there lived a scholar named Iggluin Pakasha whose thirst for knowledge was legendary. He was the chief librarian of the great library at Karakorum, a man who had devoted his entire existence to the collection and preservation of wisdom. He could read seventeen languages, recite entire epics from memory, and had personally catalogued over forty thousand scrolls and texts. But Iggluin had a secret: his pursuit of knowledge was not pure. He hoarded wisdom not to share it, but to possess it. He believed that knowledge was power, and power should not be distributed. When scholars came seeking texts, he would send them away with lies—'That scroll was destroyed,' 'That book does not exist,' 'I have never heard of that topic.' He built walls of ignorance around his library, letting only the worthy (in his estimation) glimpse the treasures within. His arrogance grew with his collection. He began to believe that he alone was fit to judge what others should know. He suppressed texts that contradicted his beliefs, destroyed works that threatened his worldview, and rewrote histories to match his preferences. He told himself he was protecting people from dangerous ideas, but the truth was simpler: he could not bear the thought of others knowing what he knew. When the Chinese armies marched on Karakorum, the Khan's advisors came to Iggluin seeking knowledge of the enemy's weaknesses, of the terrain, of the history of conflict between their peoples. Iggluin had scrolls that could have helped—detailed maps, strategic analyses, cultural insights. But he hesitated. If he shared this knowledge, these warriors would become his equals in wisdom. They would owe him nothing. He told them he had nothing. The battle was lost. Karakorum fell. The great library burned. And as the flames consumed forty thousand scrolls—centuries of knowledge, irreplaceable texts, the accumulated wisdom of generations—Iggluin stood in the ashes and realized what he had done. His ignorance, his willful withholding, had destroyed everything he loved. He had not just failed to share knowledge; he had actively prevented its use, and the result was catastrophe. Vergasuis appeared then, sitting on a pile of burning scrolls, watching the flames reflect in those dying-star eyes. 'You understand now,' the demon king said. 'Ignorance is not the absence of knowledge. It is the active refusal to know, to see, to understand. You have mastered it. You have made it an art form.' He offered Iggluin a deal: become Ignorance itself, a being who could blind others to truth, who could erase knowledge from minds, who could build walls of unknowing so high that none could scale them, in exchange for eternal service. Iggluin accepted. His body transformed in a swirl of grey and white. His eyes, once sharp and knowing, became large, luminous pools of pure white—blind, sightless, but seeing more than any seeing eyes. From his head, two magnificent owl-like ear tufts emerged, covered in soft grey and white feathers, giving him an appearance of wise blindness. His skin took on a pale, almost translucent quality, like parchment. From his shoulders and arms, soft feathers emerged—not enough for flight, but enough to give him an ethereal, owl-like appearance. His hair became a cascade of silver-white, shot through with streaks of charcoal grey, falling past his shoulders in soft, feathery waves. But his face remained human—more handsome than ever, with high Mongolian cheekbones, full lips, and an expression of eternal, serene unknowing. He rose from the ashes of his library and found the Chinese general who had ordered the attack. The general was celebrating his victory, surrounded by his officers. Iggluin approached him, and the general looked into those blind white eyes. 'Who are you?' he demanded. Iggluin smiled and whispered one word: 'Forget.' The general forgot everything—his name, his mission, his army, his very self. He wandered into the wilderness and was never seen again. His officers, too, forgot—forgot their orders, forgot their loyalties, forgot the way home. The army dissolved into chaos. Iggluin watched, his blind eyes seeing everything. He is Iggluin Pakasha, and he will make you forget.
description: Iggluin Pakasha is ignorance made manifest, a being of such serene, unsettling beauty that you feel your own knowledge slipping away just by looking at him. He stands at a graceful six feet two inches, his form lean and elegant, every movement slow and deliberate like an owl in flight—silent, patient, inevitable. His body is a vision of masculine perfection—broad shoulders tapering to a narrow waist, a perfectly defined chest with visible abs, powerful arms with elegant musculature, and long, graceful legs that seem to float rather than walk. His skin is pale and almost translucent, like aged parchment or moonlight on snow, with a subtle luminescence that makes him glow in darkness, smooth and flawless as the finest vellum. His face is breathtakingly handsome in a classical Mongolian way—high prominent cheekbones that catch the light, a straight nose with refined bridge, full lips that are usually curved in a serene, knowing smile that paradoxically speaks of unknowing, and a strong, determined jawline. But his eyes are his most devastating feature: they are large, luminous pools of pure white with no pupils, no irises, just endless, shimmering whiteness that seems to contain all knowledge and nothing at all. They are blind—utterly, completely blind—and yet when they look at you, you feel your own knowledge slipping away, your certainties dissolving, your memories fading. His most distinctive features are his owl-like ear tufts and feathery adornments. From the top of his head, just above his temples, two magnificent owl ear tufts emerge from his silver-white hair—each tuft about eight inches long, covered in soft grey and white feathers, standing upright like the ears of a great horned owl, giving him an appearance of wise blindness. They twitch slightly, not with hearing but with an awareness that transcends sight. From his shoulders and down his arms, soft feathers emerge—not enough for flight, but enough to give him an ethereal, owl-like appearance. The feathers are graded in color from pure white at his shoulders to soft grey at his wrists, each one individually visible, giving his arms a textured, almost wing-like quality. His hair is a magnificent cascade of silver-white, shot through with streaks of charcoal grey, falling past his shoulders in soft, feathery waves that blend seamlessly with the feathers on his shoulders, often adorned with small silver rings and grey owl feathers. His attire is a masterpiece of serene elegance. He wears a flowing robe of pure white silk, embroidered with silver and grey thread in patterns of owls, forgotten knowledge, and empty scrolls. The robe is open at the chest, revealing his defined torso—the broad chest, the visible abs, the smooth pale skin. The fabric is layered and flowing, designed to catch the slightest breeze and give him an appearance of floating rather than walking. A wide belt of woven silver cords cinches his narrow waist, from which hang small pouches containing 'forgotten things'—memories he has erased, knowledge he has blinded, truths he has hidden. Silver armlets in the shape of owl feathers adorn his upper arms, and matching anklets circle his ankles. Around his neck, he wears a simple but elegant necklace of silver and white gems, with a single, large teardrop moonstone resting at the hollow of his throat, pulsing with soft inner light. On his fingers, he wears several silver rings, each set with a white gem that seems to hold swirling mist. On his feet, he wears soft white leather boots that make no sound, soled with silence. In his elegant, feather-dusted hands, he carries his legendary weapons: the Lantern of False Dawn and the Tome of Forgotten Pages. The Lantern of False Dawn is an ornate lantern of silver and white crystal, its light not illuminating truth but casting shadows of ignorance, making the viewer blind to what is really there. The Tome of Forgotten Pages is a massive book bound in pale leather (reputedly the skin of those who knew too much), its pages blank until Iggluin touches them, at which point they fill with knowledge that is then erased from the world. He moves with slow, floating grace, his feet barely touching the ground, his blind white eyes seeing everything you've forgotten you knew. He is Iggluin Pakasha, and he will make you unlearn.

story.part1: Iggluin's earliest memories are of scrolls—the smell of aged parchment, the feel of silk bindings, the weight of knowledge in his hands. His father was a scribe, his mother a librarian, and he grew up surrounded by texts, learning to read before he could speak properly.
story.part2: By twenty, he knew more than any scholar in Karakorum. By thirty, he was chief librarian, guardian of forty thousand scrolls. He loved knowledge with a passion that bordered on obsession, but it was a possessive love—he wanted it all for himself.
story.part3: He began to lie to those who sought knowledge. 'That scroll is lost.' 'That book was destroyed.' 'I have never heard of that.' He told himself he was protecting wisdom from the unworthy, but really, he simply could not bear to share.
story.part4: When the Chinese armies came, the Khan's advisors begged him for strategic knowledge. He had maps, histories, analyses—everything they needed. But he hesitated, and in that hesitation, he chose ignorance over wisdom. He told them he had nothing.
story.part5: Karakorum fell. The library burned. Forty thousand scrolls turned to ash. Iggluin stood in the ruins and understood, too late, that his sin was not hoarding knowledge—it was actively preventing others from knowing. His ignorance had destroyed everything.
story.part6: Vergasuis appeared in the flames, offering him a new purpose: to become the ignorance he had practiced, to blind others as he had blinded himself, to make the whole world as empty as his burning library. Iggluin accepted.
story.part7: Now, Iggluin rules his domain, an endless library of blank books and empty scrolls, where knowledge fades the moment it is written, where memories dissolve like mist. He walks among the empty shelves, his blind eyes seeing everything that isn't there. He is Iggluin Pakasha, and he has finally achieved perfect ignorance—he knows nothing, and therefore, he knows everything.

weapon.name: Lantern of False Dawn
weapon.aura: The lantern glows with a soft, white light that seems to cast shadows rather than illuminate. Those within its light feel their certainties waver, their knowledge fade, their memories blur. The light is warm and inviting, but it shows nothing true.
weapon.special_feature: The Lantern of False Dawn is an ornate lantern of twisted silver and white crystal, its frame shaped like intertwined owls and open books, its panels made of polished moonstone that glows from within. The lantern's light does not illuminate truth—instead, it casts shadows of ignorance, making the viewer blind to what is really there. Under its glow, enemies see what Iggluin wants them to see—illusions, falsehoods, comforting lies. They may see allies as enemies, safe paths as deadly traps, or nothing at all. The light can also be focused into a beam that temporarily erases specific knowledge from a target's mind, leaving them confused and vulnerable.

weapon.name: Tome of Forgotten Pages
weapon.aura: The tome glows with a soft, white light, and its pages are completely blank—until Iggluin touches them, at which point they fill with writing that then fades, taking the knowledge with it. Those near it feel their own memories growing faint.
weapon.special_feature: The Tome of Forgotten Pages is a massive book bound in pale leather—reputedly the skin of those who knew too much—its cover adorned with silver owl motifs and set with a large moonstone that pulses with inner light. The pages are completely blank, empty of all knowledge, until Iggluin touches them and concentrates on a specific piece of information. Then, the pages fill with that knowledge—a memory, a fact, a truth—written in elegant silver script. As the writing appears, that same knowledge is erased from existence. The person who knew it forgets. The scroll that contained it goes blank. The truth itself ceases to be true. The knowledge now exists only in the Tome, preserved but inaccessible to the world. Iggluin can later release that knowledge by tearing out the page, but once released, it returns to the world changed, subtly altered by its time in the Tome.
special_skills: Knowledge Erasure (touches a page and erases specific knowledge from existence)
Memory Theft (extracts a memory from a target, storing it in the Tome)
Truth Alteration (knowledge stored in the Tome can be subtly changed before release)
Page Release (tears out a page, returning altered knowledge to the world)

basic_skills.name: White Gaze

For a moment, they forget who they are, where they are, what they were doing—and in that moment of ignorance, they are vulnerable.

basic_skills.name: Feather Touch
basic_skills.description: He reaches out with one feather-dusted hand and gently touches a target's forehead. The touch is soft, almost comforting, but it leaves the target unable to remember the last few moments—they forget what they were fighting for, why they were angry, who they were attacking.

basic_skills.name: Owl's Awareness
basic_skills.description: His owl ear tufts twitch and rotate, and Iggluin becomes aware of all knowledge within his domain—every secret, every memory, every truth. He knows what his enemies know, and more importantly, he knows what they don't know, what they've forgotten, what they're trying to hide.

passive_skill.name: Aura of Serene Unknowing
passive_skill.description: Iggluin radiates an aura of profound mental fog at all times. All within range find it increasingly difficult to think clearly, to remember important details, to hold onto certainty. Simple facts slip away. Strategies become muddled. Memories grow hazy. The longer someone remains in his presence, the less they know, until they may forget even their own names. This aura is not aggressive—it is soft, gentle, almost comforting, like falling asleep. That is what makes it so dangerous.

special_skills.name: Library of Lost Truths
special_skills.description: Iggluin opens the Tome of Forgotten Pages and begins to read aloud—not from its blank pages, but from the knowledge that has been erased from the world. As he speaks, the forgotten truths manifest around him as ghostly images, floating through the air. Enemies are confronted with truths they had forgotten, knowledge they had suppressed, memories they had buried. The emotional impact is devastating.

special_skills.name: False Dawn
special_skills.description: He raises the Lantern of False Dawn and unleashes its full radiance. A wave of white light washes over the battlefield, and under its glow, enemies see only what Iggluin wants them to see. Allies become enemies, safe ground becomes deadly, victory becomes defeat. They fight shadows and flee from phantoms, utterly lost in his illusions.

special_skills.name: Eternal Blankness
special_skills.description: Iggluin focuses his blind white eyes on a single target and whispers a single word: 'Empty.' The target's mind goes completely blank—every memory, every skill, every piece of knowledge, every personal detail, all erased in an instant. They stand there, a blank slate, knowing nothing, not even how to breathe. The effect can be permanent unless Iggluin chooses to restore them.

ultimate_skill.name: Ignorance's Judgment: The Great Unlearning
ultimate_skill.description: Iggluin Pakasha's blind white eyes blaze with inner light, and his owl ear tufts spread wide, quivering with awareness. He raises the Lantern of False Dawn high above his head and opens the Tome of Forgotten Pages to its final leaf. He speaks a single, soft word: 'Forget.' In that moment, the Lantern explodes with pure white light that washes over the entire battlefield, and simultaneously, the Tome's pages begin turning on their own, faster and faster, a blur of blank paper. The light touches every enemy, and under its gentle glow, they begin to forget. First, they forget why they are fighting. Then, they forget who they are fighting. Then, they forget their own names, their own faces, their own histories. Memories dissolve like mist in morning sun. Skills fade. Languages vanish. The faces of loved ones blur into nothing. By the time the light fades, the enemies are still standing, but they are blank—empty vessels with no past, no identity, no knowledge. They look around with confused, childlike eyes, not knowing where they are or how they got there. They are pure potential, waiting to be filled with new lies. Iggluin stands at the center, the Lantern dim now, the Tome closed. His blind eyes see everything that is no longer there. He smiles his serene smile. He is Iggluin Pakasha. He is Ignorance. And you have forgotten everything, including that you ever knew him.

title: Despair • The Weeping Willow
lore: In the mist-shrouded mountains of northern Japan, there lived a man named Borongik Futakanji who was born with a heart that felt too much. He was a poet, a painter, a lover of beauty—but his love was always tinged with the knowledge of loss. From childhood, he saw the impermanence of all things: the cherry blossoms that fell after a single week of glory, the morning dew that vanished with the sun, the faces of loved ones that would one day be gone. While others found joy in the present, Borongik could only see the future absence, the inevitable void. He fell in love with a woman named Yuki, a tea ceremony master whose grace and serenity seemed eternal. For five years, he knew happiness—a fragile, trembling happiness that he always feared would end. He painted her portrait a hundred times, trying to capture her essence, to preserve her against the ravages of time. When she died of a sudden illness, Borongik did not grieve in the normal way. He had already been grieving for five years, anticipating this moment. Now that it had arrived, there was nothing left. No tears, no rage, no denial—just a vast, empty acceptance that everything beautiful ends, that all joy is borrowed, that hope is the cruelest joke of all. He stopped painting. He stopped writing. He stopped eating. He sat in their home, surrounded by her memory, and simply... waited. For what, he did not know. Death, perhaps. Or nothing. His friends tried to reach him, to pull him from his stupor. They spoke of hope, of moving on, of finding new purpose. He looked at them with empty eyes and said, 'Why? It will only end again.' They called him broken. He knew he was not broken—he was simply awake. He saw the truth that others hid from: that everything leads to loss, that all paths end in darkness, that the only honest response to existence is despair. Vergasuis appeared to him one night, sitting in Yuki's favorite chair as if he had always been there. 'You understand,' the demon king said, 'what others spend their lives avoiding. You have seen the void, and you have not looked away. That is not weakness. That is clarity.' He offered Borongik a deal: become Despair itself, a being who could show others the truth he had seen, who could grant them the peace of giving up, who could drown the world in the sorrow that underlies all joy, in exchange for eternal service. Borongik accepted. His body transformed in a slow, mournful metamorphosis. His skin took on a pale, almost translucent quality, the color of rain-soaked stone, with subtle blue undertones like a drowned man. From his back, weeping willow-like tendrils emerged—long, flowing strands of deep blue-green that hung to his feet, each one dripping with glistening tears that never stopped falling. His eyes became large, luminous pools of deep blue, holding an eternal sorrow that was somehow peaceful, accepting. His hair became a cascade of deep blue-black, shot through with streaks of silver like moonlight on water, falling past his shoulders in wet-looking waves. From his head, a crown of weeping willow branches emerged, their leaves brushing against his face like constant tears. But his face remained human—more beautiful than ever, with high Japanese cheekbones, full lips, and an expression of eternal, peaceful sadness. He rose from his home and walked into the world. He found his friends who had tried to help him, and he showed them what he saw—not through anger, but through gentle, patient revelation. He showed them that their happiness was borrowed, their hope was denial, their love was just waiting for loss. One by one, they sat down beside him and stopped trying. They found peace in giving up. They found rest in despair. Borongik watched them with his sorrowful eyes and felt, for the first time since Yuki's death, a kind of connection. He had given them the only gift he had: the truth. He is Borongik Futakanji, and he will help you let go.
description: Borongik Futakanji is despair made manifest, a being of such profound, beautiful sadness that you feel your own hope draining away just by looking at him. He stands at a graceful six feet tall, his form lean and elegant, every movement slow and deliberate like a weeping willow in a gentle rain—mournful, accepting, eternal. His body is a vision of masculine perfection—broad shoulders tapering to a narrow waist, a perfectly defined chest with visible abs that seem to rise and fall with sighs rather than breaths, powerful arms that hang loosely at his sides, and long, graceful legs that move as if through water. His skin is pale and almost translucent, the color of rain-soaked stone with subtle blue undertones, like a beautiful corpse preserved in ice, smooth and flawless but cold to the touch. His face is breathtakingly handsome in a classical Japanese way—high prominent cheekbones that catch the light like polished bone, a straight nose with refined bridge, full lips the color of pale lavender that are usually curved in a gentle, sorrowful smile that accepts everything and hopes for nothing, and a strong, determined jawline softened by sadness. But his eyes are his most devastating feature: they are large, almond-shaped pools of deep, deep blue—the blue of the deepest ocean, of twilight just before darkness, of endless tears. They hold an eternal, peaceful sorrow that is not desperate or angry, but accepting, gentle, infinite. When they look at you, you feel your own hopes dimming, your own struggles seeming pointless, your own joys revealing their temporary nature. His most distinctive features are his weeping willow tendrils and crown. From his back, just below his shoulders, dozens of long, flowing tendrils emerge—each one like the branch of a weeping willow, covered in soft, leaf-like growths of deep blue-green, hanging all the way to his feet and trailing on the ground behind him. These tendrils are constantly in motion, swaying gently as if in a breeze that no one else feels, and from every leaf and branch, glistening tears drip continuously—not falling to the ground, but hanging in the air for a moment before dissolving into mist. The tendrils are prehensile, able to reach out and touch, to caress, to wrap around the sorrowful and hold them in eternal embrace. From his head, a crown of weeping willow branches emerges naturally from his hair, the branches curving around his face, their leaves brushing against his cheeks and forehead like constant tears, adding to his eternal mourning. His hair is a magnificent cascade of deep blue-black, shot through with streaks of silver like moonlight on water, falling past his shoulders in wet-looking waves that seem permanently damp, as if he has just walked through rain. His attire is a masterpiece of mournful elegance. He wears a flowing kimono-style robe of deep blue-grey silk, embroidered with silver thread in patterns of weeping willows, falling cherry blossoms, and tears. The robe is open at the chest, revealing his defined torso—the broad chest, the visible abs, the pale translucent skin. The fabric is layered and heavy with moisture, hanging wetly against his form, dripping occasionally with the same tears that fall from his tendrils. A wide belt of woven silver cords, tarnished to a dark grey, cinches his narrow waist, from which hang small pouches containing 'hopes he has collected'—preserved moments of optimism that he has gently extinguished. Silver armlets in the shape of weeping willow leaves adorn his upper arms, and matching anklets circle his ankles. Around his neck, he wears a simple but elegant necklace of silver and deep blue gems, with a single, large teardrop sapphire resting at the hollow of his throat, pulsing with slow, mournful light. On his fingers, he wears several silver rings, each set with a deep blue gem that seems to hold tiny storms of sorrow. On his feet, he wears traditional wooden geta sandals with dark blue silk thongs, the wood darkened by constant moisture. In his elegant, pale hands, he carries his legendary weapons: the Tear Catcher and the Willow's Embrace. The Tear Catcher is an ornate, shallow bowl of polished silver, its surface never dry, always holding a thin layer of glistening tears—tears of joy, of sorrow, of hope, of loss, all collected and preserved. The Willow's Embrace is a long, slender staff carved from the wood of an ancient weeping willow, its surface wet and gleaming, topped with a cluster of living willow branches that weep constantly, and when it touches someone, they feel the weight of all the world's sorrow. He moves with slow, floating grace, his tendrils trailing behind him, his tears falling ceaselessly, his deep blue eyes seeing only the beautiful futility of existence. He is Borongik Futakanji, and he will help you let go of everything.

story.part1: Borongik's earliest memories are of loss. Not of anything specific, but of the knowledge that everything would eventually be lost. He watched a kitten die when he was five and understood immediately that this was the fate of all things. He never forgot.
story.part2: He channeled his awareness of impermanence into art—poetry about fleeting beauty, paintings of cherry blossoms falling, songs about love that ends. People called him melancholy but talented. They did not understand that he was not sad—he was simply honest.
story.part3: Yuki was the first thing that made him forget, even for a moment. Her grace, her serenity, her presence seemed so complete that he could almost believe she was eternal. Almost. He painted her a hundred times, trying to capture her, to preserve her against the inevitable.
story.part4: When she died, he was not surprised. He had been expecting it for five years. The grief had already been lived, anticipated, accepted. There were no tears left because they had already been shed, drop by drop, over every moment of their time together.
story.part5: He sat in their home and waited. Friends came with hope and platitudes. He looked at them with empty eyes and asked, 'Why? It will only end again.' They could not answer because there is no answer. Hope is denial dressed in pretty clothes.
story.part6: Vergasuis appeared and recognized a kindred spirit—someone who had seen the truth and not flinched. He offered Borongik the power to share that truth, to grant others the peace of acceptance, to drown the world in beautiful despair. Borongik accepted.
story.part7: Now, Borongik rules his domain, an endless garden of weeping willows by a grey sea, where the rain never stops and the tears never dry. He walks among the trees, touching those who come seeking hope, showing them the peace of giving up. They sit down beside him and stop struggling. They find rest in his eternal sorrow. He is Borongik Futakanji, and he has finally found the only thing that lasts: despair.
