facial_structure.nose: Straight with a refined bridge, classical Japanese beauty, high and elegant
facial_structure.lips: Full and well-defined, the color of pale lavender, usually curved in a gentle sorrowful smile that accepts everything and hopes for nothing

hair.hairstyle: A magnificent cascade of deep blue-black, shot through with streaks of silver like moonlight on water, falling past his shoulders in wet-looking waves that seem permanently damp, as if he has just walked through rain
hair.hair_color: Deep blue-black with silver streaks

facial_structure.ears: Normal human ears, partly hidden by his weeping willow crown and wet hair, adorned with small silver teardrop earrings
facial_structure.face_shape: Classical Japanese beauty with high prominent cheekbones that catch the light like polished bone, a strong determined jawline softened by sadness, and perfect symmetry that is both beautiful and heartbreaking

upper_body.body_structure: Lean and elegant at six feet tall, with a perfectly defined masculine physique—broad shoulders tapering to a narrow waist, defined chest with visible abs that seem to rise and fall with sighs rather than breaths, powerful arms that hang loosely, every movement slow and mournful
upper_body.arms: Powerful, elegant arms, covered in pale translucent skin with blue undertones, hanging loosely at his sides, ending in pale hands with long fingers that seem perpetually ready to receive tears
upper_body.hands: His hands are pale and elegant, the long fingers slightly damp, always open as if catching rain or tears, capable of gentle caresses that transfer despair or precise gestures that summon sorrow
upper_body.chest: Broad and perfectly defined, with visible pectorals and a six-pack of abdominal muscles on full display through the open front of his wet silk robe, the pale translucent skin with blue undertones gleaming with moisture
upper_body.shoulders: Broad and elegant, from which his dozens of weeping willow tendrils emerge, cascading down his back, the muscles beneath perfectly defined
upper_body.neck: Long and graceful, adorned with the simple silver and sapphire necklace that draws the eye to the hollow of his throat, where a single tear often rests

lower_body.hips: Narrow and elegant, cinched by the tarnished silver cord belt from which hang small pouches of collected hopes
lower_body.legs: Long, graceful legs, partially visible through the wet layers of his kimono, their skin pale and translucent, the muscles elegantly defined, moving slowly as if through water
lower_body.feet: Long, elegant feet encased in traditional wooden geta sandals with dark blue silk thongs, the wood darkened by constant moisture, appearing to float just above the ground rather than walk upon it

clothing: Borongik wears a flowing kimono-style robe of deep blue-grey silk, embroidered with silver thread in intricate patterns of weeping willows, falling cherry blossoms, and tears. The robe is open at the chest, revealing his defined torso—the broad chest, the visible abs, the pale translucent skin. The fabric is layered and heavy with moisture, hanging wetly against his form, dripping occasionally with the same tears that fall from his tendrils. A wide belt of woven silver cords, tarnished to a dark grey, cinches his narrow waist, from which hang small silver pouches containing 'hopes he has collected'—preserved moments of optimism that he has gently extinguished.
accessories: Small silver teardrop earrings; a simple silver and sapphire necklace with a teardrop sapphire at his throat; the tarnished silver cord belt with small pouches; silver weeping willow leaf armlets and anklets; several silver rings with deep blue gems holding tiny storms of sorrow; traditional wooden geta sandals with dark blue silk thongs.

weapon.name: Tear Catcher
weapon.aura: The bowl glows with a soft, blue-silver light, and its surface is never dry—always holding a thin layer of glistening tears. Those near it feel their own eyes pricking with unshed sorrow, their own griefs rising to the surface.
weapon.special_feature: The Tear Catcher is an ornate, shallow bowl of polished silver, its surface etched with weeping willows and falling tears, its rim set with small sapphires that pulse with mournful light. The bowl is never empty—it always holds a thin layer of glistening tears, collected from countless sources: tears of joy, of sorrow, of hope, of loss, of relief, of despair. Borongik can use these tears in many ways. He can concentrate them into a single, devastating drop that contains all the world's sorrow, capable of overwhelming even the strongest spirit. He can release them as a mist that fills an area with melancholy. He can drink them to fuel his power, each tear adding to his eternal despair. The bowl also allows him to collect new tears—any tears shed within his presence flow toward it, adding to his collection.
special_skills: Sorrow Drop (concentrates all collected tears into a single devastating drop of pure despair)
Melancholy Mist (releases tears as a mist that fills an area with sorrow)
Tear Drink (consumes tears to fuel his power and heal his sorrow)
Grief Collection (any tears shed within his presence flow into the bowl)

weapon.name: Willow's Embrace
weapon.aura: The staff glows with a soft, blue-green light, and its weeping branches constantly drip with tears. Those near it feel the weight of all the world's sorrow pressing down on them, making their own troubles seem small and meaningless.
weapon.special_feature: The Willow's Embrace is a long, slender staff carved from the wood of an ancient weeping willow that grew on the banks of the river Styx, its surface wet and gleaming with eternal moisture. The staff is topped with a cluster of living willow branches that weep constantly, their tears running down the staff and pooling at its base. When the staff touches someone—whether in combat or in comfort—it transfers the weight of all the sorrow it has absorbed into that person. They feel not just their own griefs, but the collective despair of everyone Borongik has ever touched, everyone whose tears have been collected, everyone who has given up. The effect is paralyzing, overwhelming, and strangely peaceful. The staff can also be used to create barriers of woven willow branches, to strike with the force of crashing waves, or to gently guide the hopeless toward final rest.
special_skills: Sorrow Transfer (touches a target, transferring the weight of all collected sorrow)
Willow Wall (creates a barrier of living willow branches that weep and mourn)
Crashing Wave Strike (strikes with the force of a tidal wave of grief)
Gentle Guidance (the staff guides the hopeless toward peaceful surrender)

basic_skills.name: Blue Gaze
basic_skills.description: Borongik fixes his deep blue, sorrowful eyes on a target. The target feels their own hidden griefs rising to the surface—losses they thought they had moved past, fears they had buried, hopes they had secretly abandoned. They are momentarily paralyzed by the weight of their own sorrow.

basic_skills.name: Tendril Touch
basic_skills.description: One of his weeping willow tendrils reaches out and gently brushes against a target. The touch is soft, wet, and strangely comforting, but it leaves the target feeling the beginnings of despair—a sense that their struggles are pointless, that giving up would be easier, that rest is better than hope.

basic_skills.name: Tear Drop
basic_skills.description: He flicks a single tear from the Tear Catcher toward a target. The tear flies through the air and strikes them, and for a moment, they experience all the sorrow contained in that one drop—a lifetime of grief compressed into an instant.

passive_skill.name: Aura of Eternal Sorrow
passive_skill.description: Borongik radiates an aura of profound, peaceful despair at all times. All within range feel their hopes dimming, their struggles seeming less important, their joys revealing their temporary nature. This is not an aggressive aura—it is gentle, comforting, almost inviting. The longer someone remains in his presence, the more they begin to accept that giving up is not weakness but wisdom. They find themselves wanting to sit down, to rest, to stop trying. Suicide rates in areas he passes through spike, but the deaths are peaceful, almost grateful.

special_skills.name: Garden of Weeping Willows
special_skills.description: Borongik raises the Willow's Embrace and drives it into the ground. Instantly, dozens of weeping willow trees sprout from the earth, surrounding the battlefield in a dense forest of sorrow. Each tree weeps constantly, and their tears fill the air with a mist of melancholy. Enemies become lost in the forest, wandering aimlessly, their will to fight draining away with every tear that touches them.

special_skills.name: Ocean of Tears
special_skills.description: He tips the Tear Catcher and releases all the tears it contains in a controlled flood. A wave of glistening liquid sorrow washes across the battlefield, and any it touches is flooded with despair. They don't drown physically—they drown emotionally, overwhelmed by grief, unable to breathe for sorrow.

special_skills.name: Eternal Embrace
special_skills.description: Borongik's dozens of weeping willow tendrils reach out simultaneously, wrapping around a target in a gentle, inescapable cocoon of wet branches and falling tears. The target is held close, surrounded by sorrow, and as the tendrils weep on them, they slowly, peacefully, give up. Their struggles cease. Their eyes close. They find rest in his embrace.

ultimate_skill.name: Despair's Judgment: The Peace That Passeth Understanding
ultimate_skill.description: Borongik Futakanji's deep blue eyes blaze with the light of a thousand drowned souls, and his weeping willow tendrils spread wide, reaching toward the sky like the branches of a cosmic tree. He raises the Tear Catcher high above his head and drives the Willow's Embrace into the ground before him. He speaks a single, soft word: 'Rest.' In that moment, the tears in the Tear Catcher rise into the air, forming a vast, swirling ocean above the battlefield—an ocean of every tear ever shed, every grief ever felt, every sorrow ever endured. The Willow's Embrace grows, its branches stretching to the sky, connecting earth to that ocean of tears. And then it begins to rain. Not ordinary rain, but tears—glistening, sorrowful tears that fall on every enemy, every ally, every living thing. And as the tears touch them, they feel it: the weight of all the world's sorrow, all at once, but presented not as torment but as truth. They see that their struggles are temporary, their hopes are borrowed, their joys are fleeting. They see that in the end, everything returns to sorrow, and that is not a tragedy—it is just the way of things. And in that seeing, they find peace. They stop fighting. They stop running. They stop hoping. They simply stand there, letting the tears wash over them, accepting everything, resisting nothing. Their faces relax into expressions of serene surrender. Their weapons fall from limp hands. They are not dead—they are beyond death. They have found the peace that comes from absolute acceptance. Borongik stands at the center, the rain of tears falling around him, his tendrils swaying gently, his eyes soft and sorrowful. He looks at the battlefield of peacefully surrendered souls and smiles his gentle, sorrowful smile. He has given them the only gift that matters: the truth. He is Borongik Futakanji. He is Despair. And finally, everyone can rest.

title: Injustice • The Iron Scales
nickname: She Who Weighs Hearts and Finds Them Wanting
lore: In the rigid courts of the Joseon dynasty, there lived a woman named Jeirgani Furumu whose sense of justice was absolute. She was the daughter of a magistrate, a man who prided himself on his fairness, his adherence to the law, his incorruptible judgment. Jeirgani grew up in the shadow of her father's courtroom, watching him dispense justice with what seemed like wisdom and compassion. She believed in him absolutely. She believed in the law absolutely. When a powerful nobleman was brought before her father, accused of a brutal crime against a peasant family, Jeirgani was certain justice would be done. The evidence was clear. The nobleman's guilt was undeniable. But that night, she overheard her father speaking with the nobleman's representatives. Bags of gold changed hands. Promises of advancement were whispered. The next day, her father declared the nobleman innocent, blamed the peasant family for lying, and had the father executed for false accusation. Jeirgani's world shattered. She confronted her father, and he looked at her with cold eyes and said, 'Justice is what those with power say it is. You will learn this, or you will suffer.' She did not learn. She could not learn. The injustice of it burned in her like a fire that would never die. She began to document every corrupt judgment she witnessed, every bribe taken, every innocent punished, every guilty freed. Her father discovered her records and had her arrested, charged with treason against the family name. She was sentenced to death. On the night before her execution, as she sat in her cold cell, Vergasuis appeared to her. He did not offer comfort or rescue. He offered something better: the power to make justice what she said it was. He offered her the chance to become Injustice itself—not the absence of justice, but the power to define it, to weigh hearts and find them wanting, to tip the scales however she chose. Jeirgani accepted. Her body transformed in a cascade of iron and gold. Her skin took on a metallic sheen, like polished iron with gold inlay, smooth and unyielding. From her back, a massive set of iron scales emerged—not carried, but part of her, extending above her head like a macabre halo, their chains connecting to her shoulders and spine. Her eyes became large, luminous pools of molten gold, holding an eternal, calculating judgment that weighed everything and everyone. Her hair became a cascade of iron-grey shot through with gold, falling past her waist in sharp, geometric waves. Iron and gold armor plates grew from her skin, covering her shoulders, her arms, her hips—not worn, but part of her, natural as scales. But her face remained human—more beautiful than ever, with high Korean cheekbones, full lips painted gold, and an expression of cold, absolute authority. She rose from her cell and walked through the prison, and the walls bent to her will. She found her father in his chambers, counting his gold. She stood before him, her iron scales towering above her, her gold eyes burning. 'You taught me that justice is what those with power say it is,' she said. 'Now I have power.' She weighed his heart on her scales, and it came up light—so light it barely registered. She sentenced him to the same fate he had given so many innocents. And she smiled, because for the first time, the scales were hers to tip. Now, Jeirgani rules her domain, an endless courtroom where every soul is tried, every heart is weighed, and every verdict is whatever she decides. She is Jeirgani Furumu, and she is the only judge you will ever need.
description: Jeirgani Furumu is injustice made manifest, a being of such cold, absolute beauty that you feel judged the moment you lay eyes on her. She stands at an imperious six feet tall, her form powerful and statuesque, every movement deliberate and authoritative like a queen ascending her throne. Her body is a vision of feminine perfection—an hourglass figure with an impossibly tiny waist, full high breasts that strain against her iron-and-gold armor, wide hips that command attention, and thick, powerful thighs that speak of unshakeable strength. Her skin is pale with a metallic sheen, like polished iron that has been inlaid with gold, smooth and unyielding to the touch, cool as metal, flawless as a forged blade. Her face is breathtakingly beautiful in a classical Korean way—high prominent cheekbones that catch the light like gilded armor, a straight nose with refined bridge, full lips painted the color of molten gold that are usually set in a thin, authoritative line, and a strong, determined jawline that speaks of absolute certainty. But her eyes are her most devastating feature: they are large, almond-shaped pools of molten gold, holding an eternal, calculating judgment that weighs everything and everyone they see. When they look at you, you feel your entire life being assessed, every action judged, every secret weighed, and you know—you absolutely know—that you will be found wanting. Her most distinctive feature is her living scales. From her upper back, just below her shoulders, a massive set of iron scales emerges—not carried, but growing from her, part of her very being. The scales are immense, each pan large enough to hold a human heart, connected by heavy iron chains that attach directly to her shoulders and spine, the chains moving and clinking with her every gesture. The central pillar of the scales rises above her head like a macabre halo, and the balance arm extends to either side, the pans hanging at shoulder level. The scales are not merely decorative—they are functional, able to weigh anything from physical objects to abstract concepts, and Jeirgani can read their verdict with absolute certainty. The scales are forged from dark iron inlaid with gold, the pans etched with images of hearts, souls, and final judgments. From various points on her body, iron and gold armor plates grow naturally from her skin—shoulder guards that curve elegantly, forearm plates that gleam, hip armor that accentuates her figure, thigh guards that protect without concealing. These are not worn; they are her, as natural as scales on a fish, as beautiful as they are deadly. Her hair is a magnificent cascade of iron-grey shot through with streaks of gold, falling past her waist in sharp, geometric waves that seem almost metallic in their precision, each strand catching light like fine wire. It is pulled back from her face in an elaborate style, held by golden pins shaped like scales of justice. Her attire is a masterpiece of authoritarian elegance. She wears a form-fitting dress of deep charcoal grey silk, but it is almost entirely covered by her natural iron-and-gold armor plates, which grow through strategic openings in the fabric. The dress is cut to accentuate her hourglass figure, with a neckline that plunges between her breasts, revealing their generous swell and the golden sheen of her skin. A wide belt of hammered gold links cinches her impossibly small waist, from which hang small pouches containing 'verdicts' she has rendered. Gold armlets in the shape of balanced scales adorn her upper arms, and matching greaves protect her shins. Around her neck, she wears a stunning collar of gold and iron, with a single, large teardrop golden amber resting at the hollow of her throat. On her fingers, she wears several gold rings, each set with a dark iron gem that seems to absorb light. On her feet, she wears high-heeled boots of polished iron and gold, their heels clicking with authority on any surface. In her elegant, metallic-shimmering hands, she carries her legendary weapons: the Gavel of Final Judgment and the Ledger of Unequal Weights. The Gavel of Final Judgment is a massive, two-handed gavel forged from solid iron with a gold striking face, its handle wrapped in black leather, and when it strikes, it renders a verdict that cannot be appealed. The Ledger of Unequal Weights is a massive book bound in iron plates, its pages made of hammered gold leaf, recording every judgment she has ever made, every heart she has weighed, every sentence she has delivered. She moves with slow, deliberate grace, her scales clinking softly behind her, her gold eyes always judging, always weighing, always finding. She is Jeirgani Furumu, and she is the law.

story.part1: Jeirgani's childhood was one of absolute faith. Her father was a magistrate, a man of justice, or so she believed. She sat in his courtroom, watched him judge, and learned that the law was sacred, that truth would always prevail, that the innocent would be protected.
story.part2: She believed this with the absolute certainty of a child who has not yet learned that adults lie. She believed it even as she saw the nobleman brought before her father, even as she heard the evidence, even as she knew—knew—that he was guilty.
story.part3: The night she overheard the bribe was the night her faith died. Bags of gold. Whispered promises. And the next day, her father declared the nobleman innocent and executed the innocent father who had accused him. She watched an innocent man die because of gold.
story.part4: When she confronted her father, he did not apologize. He did not explain. He looked at her with cold eyes and said, 'Justice is what those with power say it is. You will learn this, or you will suffer.' She did not learn. She documented.
story.part5: Her father discovered her records and had her arrested, sentenced to death for treason against the family. As she sat in her cell, she realized that he was right—justice was what those with power said it was. And she had no power. Yet.
story.part6: Vergasuis appeared and offered her the ultimate power: the ability to define justice herself, to weigh hearts and find them wanting, to be the judge, the jury, the executioner. She accepted without hesitation, and her body transformed into a living instrument of judgment.
story.part7: Now, Jeirgani rules her domain, an endless courtroom where every soul is tried. She weighs hearts on her iron scales, and they are always found wanting—not because they are guilty, but because she decides they are. She has learned her father's lesson well: justice is what those with power say it is. And she has all the power. She is Jeirgani Furumu, and the court is always in session.

powers: Heart Weighing (her iron scales can weigh any heart, any soul, any action, and give a precise measurement of its 'worth'—but the scales answer to her will, showing whatever verdict she desires), Absolute Judgment (her presence imposes the feeling of being judged, of being on trial, making enemies defensive and uncertain), Verdict Enforcement (any judgment she speaks becomes magically binding—'guilty' means guilty, 'innocent' means innocent, regardless of truth), Gold Gaze (her molten gold eyes can see through any defense, any lie, any secret, revealing the truth she will then twist), Iron Will (her metallic skin and natural armor make her nearly impervious to physical and magical attack), Scale Manipulation (her living scales can extend, contract, and strike, the chains serving as whips, the pans as shields or bludgeons), Gavel Mastery (wields the Gavel of Final Judgment to deliver verdicts that cannot be appealed), Ledger Mastery (wields the Ledger of Unequal Weights to record and enforce her judgments)
speciality: Judgment Manipulation, Verdict Enforcement, Psychological Domination, Absolute Authority

weapon.name: Gavel of Final Judgment
weapon.aura: The gavel glows with a harsh gold light, and those near it feel a verdict hanging over them, a judgment waiting to be delivered. The air around it is heavy with finality.
weapon.special_feature: The Gavel of Final Judgment is a massive, two-handed gavel forged from solid iron with a striking face of pure gold that gleams with inner light. The handle is wrapped in black leather, and the head is carved with images of scales, hearts, and final sentences. When Jeirgani strikes the gavel—against a surface, against the air, against an enemy—she delivers a verdict that cannot be appealed. If she declares 'guilty' as she strikes, the target is immediately afflicted with whatever punishment she deems appropriate—weakness, pain, paralysis, even death. If she declares 'innocent,' they are protected, healed, empowered. The gavel's power is absolute within her domain and terrifyingly effective anywhere. The sound of its strike echoes in the soul long after the physical sound fades.
special_skills: Guilty Verdict (a strike that inflicts punishment based on her judgment)
Innocent Verdict (a strike that protects or heals based on her judgment)
Courtroom Silence (a strike that silences all opposition, magical or vocal)
Final Appeal (a strike that cannot be blocked, dodged, or resisted)

weapon.name: Ledger of Unequal Weights
weapon.aura: The ledger glows with a harsh gold light, and its iron-bound covers seem to pulse with contained judgments. Those near it feel their names being written, their fates being recorded.
weapon.special_feature: The Ledger of Unequal Weights is a massive book bound in iron plates, its cover embossed with golden scales and the words 'Final Judgment' in an ancient script. Its pages are made of hammered gold leaf, thin but indestructible, and they record every judgment Jeirgani has ever made, every heart she has weighed, every sentence she has delivered. The ledger does not merely record—it enforces. Any name written in its pages is bound by the judgment recorded there. Jeirgani can add names with a touch, writing verdicts that become reality. She can also consult the ledger to review past judgments, to draw power from them, or to summon the ghosts of those she has condemned to serve as witnesses in her eternal court.
special_skills: Name Recording (writes a name and verdict, making it reality)
Judgment Review (consults past judgments to gain power or knowledge)
Witness Summon (calls forth the ghosts of the condemned to testify)
Page of Doom (tears out a page, releasing its judgment on all who read it)

basic_skills.name: Gold Gaze
basic_skills.description: Jeirgani fixes her molten gold eyes on a target. The target feels immediately judged, every action they have ever taken weighed and found wanting. They become defensive, uncertain, and susceptible to her authority.

basic_skills.name: Scale Weighing
basic_skills.description: One of her iron scale pans extends toward a target, hovering before their chest. The target feels their heart being weighed, their soul being measured, and they know—absolutely know—that they are being judged. The verdict, whatever it will be, is already decided.

basic_skills.name: Chain Lash
basic_skills.description: The chains connecting her scales lash out like iron whips, striking multiple targets. The chains do physical damage, but more importantly, they leave behind the feeling of being bound by judgment, of being sentenced, of having no appeal.

passive_skill.name: Aura of Absolute Judgment
passive_skill.description: Jeirgani radiates an aura of inescapable judgment at all times. All within range feel as if they are on trial, as if every word they speak is testimony, every action evidence, every thought subject to scrutiny. This aura makes enemies hesitant, defensive, and prone to second-guessing themselves. They feel guilty, even if they have done nothing wrong, and that guilt makes them vulnerable to her judgments.

special_skills.name: Court of Final Appeal
special_skills.description: Jeirgani raises the Gavel of Final Judgment and strikes it against the air. The sound echoes, and suddenly the battlefield transforms into her courtroom—infinite, imposing, absolute. Every enemy is seated in the defendant's chair, forced to face her judgment. She then proceeds to try them, one by one, weighing their hearts, reading their sins, delivering verdicts that become reality.

special_skills.name: Weighing of Hearts
special_skills.description: She extends both scale pans toward a target, and the target feels their heart lift from their chest and settle onto one pan—metaphorically, but painfully real. On the other pan, Jeirgani places the weight of their sins, their secrets, their failures. The scales tip, always in her favor, and the target is crushed by the weight of their own inadequacy.

special_skills.name: Page of Condemnation
special_skills.description: Jeirgani opens the Ledger of Unequal Weights to a blank page and writes a target's name. As she writes, the target feels their fate being sealed, their future being determined. When she finishes, the page glows, and the judgment she has written—'guilty of cowardice,' 'sentenced to despair,' 'found wanting'—becomes absolute truth for that target.

ultimate_skill.name: Injustice's Judgment: The Scales That Never Lie (Because They Answer to Her)
ultimate_skill.description: Jeirgani Furumu's molten gold eyes blaze with the light of a thousand final judgments, and her iron scales expand to impossible size, their chains lengthening, their pans growing large enough to hold armies. She raises the Gavel of Final Judgment high above her head and opens the Ledger of Unequal Weights to its final page. She speaks a single, absolute word: 'Guilty.' In that moment, every enemy on the battlefield feels their hearts lift from their chests and settle onto the massive scales—not physically, but metaphysically, truly. Their entire lives, every action, every thought, every secret, is weighed in an instant. And because the scales answer to Jeirgani, every single heart is found wanting. The verdict is unanimous: guilty. The sentence is whatever she decides. For some, it is despair. For others, it is weakness. For the truly unfortunate, it is oblivion. The Gavel strikes, and the sound is the last thing many of them hear. Those who survive are marked forever, their names written in the Ledger, their fates bound to her will. They will carry her judgment for the rest of their lives, always feeling guilty, always waiting for the sentence to be carried out. Jeirgani stands at the center, her scales slowly retracting, her ledger closing, her gavel lowering. She looks at the broken, guilty souls before her and smiles her cold, absolute smile. She is Jeirgani Furumu. She is Injustice. And the court will never adjourn.

title: Humility • The Swan's Grace
lore: In the tranquil countryside of ancient Korea's Silla kingdom, there lived a young woman named Fyngyilgi Forfata whose beauty was whispered about in every village, yet she herself seemed unaware of it. She was the daughter of a poor farmer, and from childhood she worked the fields alongside her father, her hands calloused, her back bent, her face often streaked with mud. While others remarked on her luminous features—her large, gentle eyes, her flawless skin, her graceful figure—she would only smile and return to her labor. She had no mirror, no vanity, no desire to be seen. What she did have was an extraordinary gift: she could see the hidden worth in others. In the beggar by the road, she saw a fallen scholar. In the grumbling merchant, she saw a man terrified of poverty. In the proud noble, she saw a child desperate for approval. She never judged, never condemned. She simply saw, and because she saw, she could help. She gave food to the hungry without recording it, comfort to the grieving without expecting thanks, wisdom to the lost without seeking credit. Her father often said, 'Daughter, you will empty our storehouse with your giving.' And she would reply, 'Then we will have room for more.' One day, a wandering monk passed through the village. He was old and frail, and Fyngyilgi offered him her own bowl of rice. He looked at her with eyes that seemed to see through her, and he said, 'You give without thought of self. But the world will not always reward such giving. There are those who would take advantage, who would crush you for your goodness.' Fyngyilgi smiled. 'Then let them crush me. I will still give.' The monk was Bijuingi Thorak in disguise, the celestial guardian who sought souls worthy of becoming virtues. He had been searching for centuries for one whose humility was so pure it could counter the Pride of Seseei Furhana. He revealed himself and offered her a choice: to remain a simple farmer, unknown and unremembered, or to become Humility incarnate, to ride a great swan into battle against the sins, to inspire true worth in others. Fyngyilgi asked only one question: 'Will I still be able to give?' Bijuingi Thorak laughed with joy. 'You will give more than you can imagine.' She accepted, and a transformation began—not of her body into something monstrous, but of her spirit into something radiant. Her skin took on a soft, pearlescent glow. Her simple clothes became a flowing robe of pure white silk, embroidered with silver swan feathers. And from the heavens descended a magnificent swan, larger than any horse, its feathers pure white with silver tips, its eyes gentle and knowing. It knelt before her, and she mounted it without hesitation. Now, Fyngyilgi rides her swan across the realms, seeking those crushed by pride, those who have forgotten their own worth, and reminding them that they are enough—not because they are seen, but because they exist.
description: Fyngyilgi Forfata is humility made radiant, a being whose beauty is not displayed but simply is, like moonlight on still water. She stands at a graceful five feet seven inches, her form the epitome of feminine perfection—an hourglass figure with a tiny waist, full high breasts that gently curve against her white silk robe, wide hips that move with fluid grace, and thick, powerful thighs that speak of her days working the fields, now enhanced by her celestial nature. Her skin is clear and flawless, with a soft pearlescent glow that seems to emanate from within, warm and inviting rather than demanding attention. Her face is breathtakingly beautiful in a classical Korean way—high, elegant cheekbones that catch light softly, a straight nose with refined bridge, full lips the color of pale pink roses, always curved in a gentle, knowing smile that holds no pride, only quiet joy. But her eyes are her most captivating feature: large, almond-shaped pools of pure, soft silver, holding an eternal calm and a depth of seeing that perceives the worth in every soul. They do not judge; they simply witness, and in their witness, they heal. Her hair is a magnificent cascade of deep black, shot through with subtle silver highlights that appear only when light catches them, falling past her waist in soft waves, often adorned with a single white swan feather tucked behind her ear. Her attire is a masterpiece of understated elegance. She wears a flowing hanbok-style robe of pure white silk, the fabric so fine it seems to float around her, embroidered with silver thread in delicate patterns of swan feathers and lotus blossoms. The robe is modest yet reveals the graceful contours of her body—the V-neckline shows just a hint of her collarbone and the upper swell of her breasts, while the waist is cinched with a wide belt of woven silver cords, emphasizing her hourglass figure. Over her shoulders, she wears a short bolero of swan feathers, each feather pure white with silver tips, rustling softly with her movements. Silver armlets in the shape of swan wings adorn her upper arms, and matching anklets circle her delicate ankles. Around her neck, she wears a simple but elegant necklace of silver and pearls, with a single teardrop pearl resting at the hollow of her throat. On her fingers, she wears several silver rings, each set with a small pearl. On her feet, she wears soft white leather boots that reach mid-calf, soled for silence. In her graceful hands, she carries her legendary weapons: the Mirror of True Reflection and the Feather of Grace. The Mirror of True Reflection is an ornate hand mirror with a frame of polished silver shaped like swan wings, its glass showing not the viewer's face but their true inner worth, their inherent dignity. The Feather of Grace is a single, impossibly long white swan feather, its shaft pure silver, which when touched to a wounded soul transfers quiet dignity and heals the wounds of pride and humiliation. Beside her always stands her spirit animal and mount: a magnificent giant swan named Aein. The swan is enormous, standing taller than a horse with a wingspan that could shade a village. Its feathers are pure white with silver tips that shimmer in light, its eyes a gentle silver like Fyngyilgi's own. A long, graceful neck curves elegantly, and when it extends its wings, they seem to encompass the sky. It moves with silent dignity, and when Fyngyilgi rides it into battle, they become a single entity of grace and power, the swan's wings creating shields of light and its beak striking with the precision of truth. Fyngyilgi moves with quiet grace, her feet barely touching the ground, her silver eyes seeing past all pretense to the worth beneath. She is Fyngyilgi Forfata, and she needs no one to see her to know she is enough.

story.part1: Fyngyilgi's earliest memories are of working beside her father in the rice paddies, her small hands planting seedlings, her face streaked with mud. She never thought of herself as beautiful or special; she was simply a farmer's daughter, and that was enough.
story.part2: Villagers would sometimes stop and stare at her, remarking on her unusual beauty. She would smile, thank them, and return to work. She had no mirror and no interest in one. What mattered was the work, the family, the community.
story.part3: She began to notice things about people—the beggar who had once been a scholar, the merchant who gave extra food to orphans when he thought no one watched. She saw worth where others saw only surface, and she began to give without expecting return.
story.part4: Her father worried she would give away everything they had. But the more she gave, the more seemed to come back—neighbors helping with harvest, strangers leaving food at their door. The universe, it seemed, responded to her quiet generosity.
story.part5: The old monk appeared on a winter evening, frail and hungry. Fyngyilgi gave him her own supper without hesitation. When he warned her of a world that would take advantage, she simply smiled. 'Then let them take. I will still give.'
story.part6: Bijuingi Thorak revealed himself and offered her a transformation. She would become Humility, ride a great swan, and face the sin of Pride itself. She asked only if she could still give. When he said yes, she accepted without hesitation.
story.part7: Now, Fyngyilgi rides her swan Aein across the realms, seeking those crushed by pride or shame. She does not fight with violence but with truth—showing each soul their inherent worth, healing the wounds of arrogance and humiliation. She is Humility, and she needs no recognition to know she is doing what she was always meant to do.

The mirror can also be used defensively, reflecting the attacks of Pride back at the attacker, showing them their own arrogance laid bare.

basic_skills.name: Silver Gaze
basic_skills.description: Fyngyilgi fixes her soft silver eyes on a target. The target feels suddenly seen, truly seen, their defenses lowering as they realize they are being witnessed without judgment. Pride and shame both dissolve in that gaze.

basic_skills.description: She extends an arm, and Aein responds—a massive wing of white and silver sweeps forward, creating a barrier of light that protects allies and gently pushes enemies back, not with force but with undeniable grace.

basic_skills.name: Gentle Touch
basic_skills.description: She reaches out with the Feather of Grace and brushes it against a target's forehead. The target feels a wave of peace, their self-doubt easing, their worth becoming obvious to them.

passive_skill.description: Fyngyilgi radiates an aura of profound calm and acceptance at all times. All within range feel safe to be themselves, to drop their pretenses, to stop performing. The proud feel their arrogance softening; the ashamed feel their self-loathing easing. This aura does not demand—it simply offers, and those who accept find peace.

special_skills.name: Swan's Grace
special_skills.description: Fyngyilgi mounts Aein, and together they rise into the air. The swan's wings spread wide, and from them cascade thousands of silver-white feathers that drift down like snow. Wherever a feather lands, it reveals truth—hidden worth, buried dignity, forgotten value. Enemies find their pretenses stripped away, allies feel their confidence restored.

special_skills.name: Mirror of the Soul
special_skills.description: She raises the Mirror of True Reflection and turns it to face a group. Each person sees not their own face but their true self—their inherent worth, their beauty, their value. The effect is overwhelming; many weep with relief, others stand taller, all are healed of the wounds pride and shame have inflicted.

special_skills.name: Feather Dance
special_skills.description: Fyngyilgi spins gracefully, the Feather of Grace extended, creating spiraling patterns of silver light. The light wraps around allies, protecting them, and around enemies, calming them. In the dance, she shows that movement need not be aggressive to be powerful.

ultimate_skill.name: Humility's Grace: The Swan's Mirror
ultimate_skill.description: Fyngyilgi Forfata's silver eyes blaze with gentle light, and Aein spreads its magnificent wings to their full span, the silver tips glowing like stars. She raises the Mirror of True Reflection high above her head, and the mirror expands, growing to immense size, its surface becoming a perfect, calm lake of silver light. She speaks a single, soft word: 'See.' In that moment, the mirror's light washes over the entire battlefield, and every soul present sees themselves as they truly are—not as they pretend to be, not as they fear they are, but as they are in their essence: worthy, valuable, enough. The proud see their arrogance as the fragile shield it is, and they let it fall. The ashamed see their worth, and they stand taller. The lost see that they were never truly lost. Enemies drop their weapons, not in surrender but in recognition. Allies embrace, not in victory but in connection. The battle ends not with death but with understanding. Fyngyilgi sits atop Aein, the swan gliding gently down to land. She smiles her gentle smile. She has not defeated anyone. She has simply shown them who they are. And that is enough. She is Fyngyilgi Forfata. She is Humility. And she needs no victory to know she has won.

title: Generosity • The Eagle's Plenty
lore: In the ancient Mongol Empire, during the reign of the Great Khan, there lived a prince named Keiloka Beibad who was known throughout the steppes for his extraordinary generosity. He was the youngest son of a powerful chieftain, raised in luxury, surrounded by wealth beyond measure. Yet from childhood, he gave everything away. His finest clothes went to servants. His prized horses went to messengers. His gold went to the poor who gathered at the palace gates. His father despaired, 'Son, you will leave yourself with nothing!' But Keiloka only smiled and said, 'Then I will have nothing to lose, and everything to gain.' As he grew, his reputation spread. Travelers spoke of the prince who would give you his own bed if you needed rest, who would share his last meal with a stranger, who never asked for repayment. Some called him foolish. Others called him saintly. He called himself simply 'one who has enough.' When his father died, Keiloka inherited the chieftainship. On his first day as leader, he opened the treasury and distributed half the wealth to every family in the tribe. His advisors were horrified. 'We will be vulnerable to attack! Our enemies will see us as weak!' Keiloka replied, 'Our strength has never been in our gold. It is in the loyalty of our people.' And indeed, when a rival tribe did attack, every able-bodied man and woman rose to defend him, not out of duty but out of love. They won not through wealth but through unity. One evening, after a long day of settling disputes and giving judgments, an old man appeared at his tent. He was dressed in rags but had eyes that held the wisdom of ages. He asked for food, and Keiloka gave him his own supper. He asked for shelter, and Keiloka offered his tent. He asked for a horse, and Keiloka gave him his finest steed. The old man revealed himself as Bijuingi Thorak. 'You give without thought,' he said. 'You do not calculate, do not count cost, do not expect return. You are the counter to Greed itself. Will you become Generosity incarnate, ride a great eagle into battle, and teach the grasping that true wealth is in giving?' Keiloka laughed with joy. 'I have been practicing my whole life for this.' He accepted, and a transformation came over him. His skin took on a warm, sun-kissed glow. His simple deel became a magnificent robe of cream and gold, embroidered with eagle feathers. And from the sky descended a colossal eagle, its feathers cream and amber, its eyes golden, its wings spanning the horizon. It landed before him and bowed its great head. Keiloka mounted without fear. Now, he rides his eagle across the realms, seeking those trapped by greed, teaching them that holding tight only empties the hands, while opening them fills the world.
description: Keiloka Beibad is generosity made flesh, a being whose very presence feels like abundance. He stands at an impressive six feet two inches, his form a vision of masculine perfection—broad shoulders tapering to a narrow waist, a perfectly defined chest with visible abs, powerful arms with elegant musculature, and long, strong legs built for riding. His skin is a warm, sun-kissed gold, smooth and flawless, radiating a gentle heat like summer sunlight. His face is breathtakingly handsome in a classical Mongolian way—high, prominent cheekbones that catch light like gilded hills, a straight nose with refined bridge, full lips the color of warm amber, always curved in an open, generous smile that welcomes all, and a strong, determined jawline softened by kindness. His eyes are large, luminous pools of warm honey-gold, holding an eternal, open-handed acceptance that makes you feel instantly welcome, instantly worthy, instantly at home. His hair is a magnificent mane of deep brown shot through with streaks of cream and gold, falling past his shoulders in thick waves, often pulled back with a leather cord adorned with eagle feathers. His attire is a masterpiece of noble generosity. He wears a traditional Mongol deel of cream-colored silk, embroidered with gold thread in patterns of eagle feathers, clouds, and open hands. The deel is open at the chest, revealing the defined muscles of his torso—the broad pectorals, the ridged abs, the V-shaped lines leading down—with just a hint of gold chains against his skin. A wide belt of hammered gold links cinches his narrow waist, from which hang small pouches that never empty, always containing exactly what someone needs. Over his shoulders, he wears a short cape of eagle feathers, each feather cream and amber with gold tips, rustling with his movements. Gold armlets in the shape of eagle wings adorn his powerful upper arms, and matching bracelets circle his wrists. Around his neck, he wears a simple but elegant necklace of gold and amber, with a single, large teardrop amber resting at the hollow of his throat. On his fingers, he wears several gold rings, each set with a warm amber gem. On his feet, he wears soft leather boots of cream-colored leather, reaching to his knees, soled for riding. In his strong, open hands, he carries his legendary weapons: the Feather of Plenty and the Eagle's Talon Shield. The Feather of Plenty is a single, massive eagle feather, cream and gold, which when offered to the deserving provides exactly what they need—food, warmth, hope, courage. The Eagle's Talon Shield is a circular shield of eagle feathers and amber, its surface gleaming with golden light, which protects the vulnerable from those who would exploit them. Beside him always stands his spirit animal and mount: a colossal eagle named Arslan. The eagle is enormous, its wingspan wider than a yurt, its feathers a stunning gradient from cream at the body to deep amber at the tips, its eyes golden and wise. When it flies, it blocks the sun, casting a shadow that is not darkness but cool relief. Its talons are massive but never harm the innocent; they only grasp what needs to be carried to safety. When Keiloka rides Arslan into battle, they become a symbol of abundance—the eagle's wings raining down feathers that become food, gold, or comfort, its cry a call to share rather than hoard. Keiloka moves with open, welcoming grace, his hands always ready to give, his eyes always seeing need, his smile always assuring that there is enough. He is Keiloka Beibad, and he has never met a stranger, only friends he hasn't given to yet.

story.part1: Keiloka's earliest memories are of giving. As a toddler, he would hand his toys to other children. As a boy, he gave his food to hungry travelers. His father worried, his mother fretted, but Keiloka only smiled and said, 'I have enough.'
story.part2: His reputation spread across the steppes. People came from far away just to witness the prince who gave everything. Some tried to take advantage, but Keiloka never seemed to mind. 'If they need it that badly,' he said, 'then it was never mine to keep.'
story.part3: When his father died, Keiloka became chieftain. His first act was to open the treasury and give half to the people. His advisors were aghast. 'We will be weak!' they cried. But Keiloka knew that true strength was in loyalty, not gold.
story.part4: The rival tribe attacked, expecting easy pickings. Instead, they found a united people who fought not for wealth but for love of their leader. The invaders were driven back, and Keiloka's tribe emerged stronger than ever.
story.part5: The old man appeared at twilight, ragged and hungry. Keiloka gave him food, shelter, and his finest horse without hesitation. The man revealed himself as Bijuingi Thorak and offered Keiloka a purpose greater than leading a tribe.
story.part6: Keiloka accepted with joy. He had always known that his giving was not weakness but a different kind of strength. Now he would give on a cosmic scale.
story.part7: Now, Keiloka rides Arslan across the realms, seeking the grasping hands of Greed and opening them, showing the hoarders that what they clutch will rot, while what they share will multiply. He is Generosity, and he gives without counting, because there is always more where that came from.

passive_skill.description: Keiloka radiates an aura of warm, generous plenty at all times. All within range feel that there is enough—enough food, enough time, enough love, enough for everyone. Greed shrivels in this aura; generosity blooms. The poor feel hope, the rich feel the urge to share, and all feel connected.

special_skills.name: Eagle's Plenty
special_skills.description: Keiloka mounts Arslan and soars above the battlefield. The eagle's wings spread wide, and from them cascade thousands of golden feathers that drift down like snow. Wherever a feather lands, it becomes exactly what that person needs—a weapon for the soldier, a bandage for the wounded, a loaf for the hungry. The battlefield becomes a place of provision rather than destruction.

special_skills.name: Open Hand
special_skills.description: Keiloka raises both hands, palms open, and golden light radiates from them. All greedy intentions in the area are exposed, and those who were hoarding feel their possessions become heavy, burdensome, until they willingly let them go. The released wealth floats in the air, then gently distributes itself to those in need.

special_skills.name: Shield of the Vulnerable
special_skills.description: He raises the Eagle's Talon Shield and expands it into a massive dome covering all innocents on the battlefield. Attacks bounce off harmlessly, and those who attack with greed find their own greed reflected back, often causing them to drop their weapons in sudden self-awareness.

ultimate_skill.name: Generosity's Gift: The Feast of Enough
ultimate_skill.description: Keiloka Beibad's golden eyes blaze with warm light, and Arslan rises to his full height, wings spreading to block out the sky. Keiloka raises the Feather of Plenty high above his head and plants the Eagle's Talon Shield in the ground before him. He speaks a single, joyful word: 'Share.' In that moment, the Feather of Plenty explodes into a million golden sparks that rain down on the battlefield. Every single person—ally and enemy alike—receives exactly what they most need. The starving receive a feast. The cold receive warmth. The lonely receive companionship. The greedy receive the sudden, overwhelming desire to give. Weapons fall from hands as enemies embrace. Hoarded treasures spill from pockets, floating through the air to find those who need them. The battlefield transforms into a celebration, a festival, a shared meal. When the light fades, no one is dead. No one is wounded. Everyone is fed, clothed, comforted, and connected. Keiloka sits atop Arslan, the eagle gliding gently down, and smiles his open, generous smile. He has not defeated anyone. He has given them what they needed, and in receiving, they have become part of his tribe. He is Keiloka Beibad. He is Generosity. And there is always enough.

title: Patience • The Tiger's Stillness
nickname: She Who Waits for the Perfect Moment
lore: In the ancient Korean kingdom of Silla, during a time of constant warring between the Three Kingdoms, there lived a princess named Pokihata Bijau. She was the eldest daughter of King Jinheung, a warrior-king who expanded Silla's borders through relentless conquest. But Pokihata was different from her father. While he believed in striking fast and hard, she believed in waiting—watching, learning, and acting only when the moment was perfect. Her father often grew frustrated with her. 'You hesitate like a deer,' he would say. 'A warrior must seize the moment!' But Pokihata would reply, 'Father, the tiger waits in stillness for hours, but when it strikes, it does not miss.' When Silla faced a massive invasion from the neighboring kingdom of Baekje, King Jinheung wanted to launch an immediate counterattack. But Pokihata counseled patience. 'Let them come deep into our territory. Let them stretch their supply lines. Let them grow overconfident. Then we strike.' The king, against his instincts, listened to his daughter. For months, they waited, retreating, giving ground, while Pokihata studied the enemy's movements, their patterns, their weaknesses. The court whispered that she was a coward, that she was letting the enemy destroy their kingdom. She endured the whispers with a calm that seemed inhuman. Finally, when the Baekje army was spread thin and exhausted, she gave the signal. The Silla forces attacked in a perfectly coordinated assault, cutting the enemy into pieces and capturing their king. After the victory, as her father celebrated, an old woman approached Pokihata. She was dressed in tattered robes, but her eyes held the depth of ages. 'You waited,' the woman said. 'You endured doubt and accusation, and you waited. That is a rare gift.' The woman was Bijuingi Thorak in disguise. She revealed herself and offered Pokihata a choice: to become Patience incarnate, to ride a great azure tiger into battle against Wrath itself, and to teach the world that waiting is not weakness but the highest form of strength. Pokihata accepted. Her skin took on a soft, luminous quality with a faint azure undertone. Her simple warrior's clothes transformed into a flowing robe of peaceful blue and white silk, embroidered with silver tiger stripes. And from the mountains descended a colossal tiger, its fur the color of a clear sky at dawn—azure white with silver stripes, its eyes calm and knowing. It padded up to her and lay down at her feet, offering its back. She mounted without fear. Now, Pokihata rides her azure tiger across the realms, seeking those consumed by Wrath, teaching them to wait, to breathe, to choose the perfect moment rather than lashing out in fury. She is the stillness before the storm, and when she moves, she does not miss.
description: Pokihata Bijau is patience made flesh, a being of such serene, controlled power that her very presence calms the frantic and steadies the impulsive. She stands at a statuesque five feet nine inches, her form the epitome of feminine perfection—an hourglass figure with an impossibly tiny waist, full high breasts that curve gracefully against her azure silk robe, wide hips that sway with deliberate, unhurried grace, and thick, powerful thighs that speak of coiled strength waiting to be unleashed. Her skin is clear and flawless, with a soft luminous quality and a faint azure undertone that catches light like morning sky. Her face is breathtakingly beautiful in a classical Korean way—high, elegant cheekbones that catch light softly, a straight nose with refined bridge, full lips the color of pale rose, always set in a calm, knowing smile that betrays no urgency, only certainty. But her eyes are her most captivating feature: large, almond-shaped pools of deep, peaceful azure, holding an eternal stillness that sees past the present into the perfect future. They do not judge; they simply observe, waiting for the moment when action becomes necessary. Her hair is a magnificent cascade of deep midnight blue, shot through with streaks of silver-white like moonlight on water, falling past her waist in smooth, straight waves, often adorned with small silver tiger-claw pins. Her attire is a masterpiece of serene elegance. She wears a flowing hanbok-style robe of azure and white silk, embroidered with silver thread in patterns of tiger stripes and still waters. The robe is modest yet reveals the graceful contours of her body—the V-neckline shows just a hint of her collarbone and the upper swell of her breasts, while the waist is cinched with a wide belt of woven silver cords, emphasizing her hourglass figure. Over her shoulders, she wears a short cape of azure and white tiger fur, each hair seeming to shimmer with its own light. Silver armlets in the shape of tiger claws adorn her upper arms, and matching anklets circle her delicate ankles. Around her neck, she wears a simple but elegant necklace of silver and azure gems, with a single, large teardrop aquamarine resting at the hollow of her throat. On her fingers, she wears several silver rings, each set with a small azure stone. On her feet, she wears soft white leather boots that reach mid-calf, soled for silence. In her graceful, poised hands, she carries her legendary weapons: the Stillness Claw and the Tiger's Breath Fan. The Stillness Claw is a single retractable claw made of pure azure light, sheathed in silver, which she extends only when the moment is perfect—and then it strikes with absolute precision. The Tiger's Breath Fan is a folding fan of azure silk and silver ribs, which when opened releases a gentle breeze that cools rage and calms fury, giving the angry time to think. Beside her always stands her spirit animal and mount: a colossal azure white tiger named Myeongho. The tiger is enormous, larger than a war elephant, its fur a stunning gradient from pure white at the belly to deep azure at the back, with silver stripes that seem to move like flowing water. Its eyes are calm pools of azure light, and its presence radiates a stillness that makes the world slow down. When it moves, it moves with deliberate, perfect grace, and when it strikes, it strikes with the patience of a mountain. Pokihata rides Myeongho into battle, and together they are the embodiment of waiting—the calm before the storm, the stillness that precedes the perfect strike. She is Pokihata Bijau, and she will wait as long as it takes.

story.part1: Pokihata's childhood was spent in the shadow of her father's war tents. While other children played, she watched soldiers drill, noting their patterns, their strengths, their flaws. She learned to see what others missed—the slight limp, the overextended reach, the moment of inattention.
story.part2: Her father despaired of her. 'A princess must be decisive!' he would roar. But Pokihata only smiled and said, 'Father, the tiger waits in stillness for hours, but when it strikes, it does not miss.'
story.part3: When the Baekje invasion came, she counseled patience while others screamed for immediate action. She endured accusations of cowardice, of treason, of weakness. She did not waver. She simply watched, and waited, and learned.
story.part4: For months, she studied the enemy—their supply lines, their patrol patterns, their moments of weakness. She knew exactly when to strike. When the moment came, her plan unfolded with perfect precision, and the enemy was destroyed.
story.part5: After the victory, an old woman approached her. 'You waited,' she said. 'You endured doubt and accusation, and you waited. That is a rare gift.' The woman revealed herself as Bijuingi Thorak and offered Pokihata a greater purpose.
story.part6: Pokihata accepted. She had always known that patience was not passivity but the highest form of power. Now she would embody that truth.
story.part7: Now, Pokihata rides Myeongho across the realms, seeking those consumed by Wrath. She does not fight them—she waits. She waits until their fury burns itself out, until they see that their anger has no target, until they are ready to listen. And then, in that perfect moment, she speaks. She is Patience, and she will wait forever if she must.

weapon.aura: The claw glows with a soft, azure light when extended, and those near it feel time slow down, every moment stretching into eternity. It leaves trails of azure light when it strikes.
weapon.special_feature: The Stillness Claw is a single retractable claw made of pure azure light, sheathed in a silver housing worn on her right hand. basic_skills.name: Azure Gaze
basic_skills.description: Pokihata fixes her peaceful azure eyes on a target. The target feels time slow down, their urgency fading, their rage cooling. They become aware of every moment stretching before them, and they realize they can wait.

basic_skills.name: Tiger's Presence
basic_skills.description: Myeongho simply lies down nearby. The tiger's stillness radiates outward, creating a zone where frantic action becomes impossible. Enemies find themselves slowing down, hesitating, waiting—just as the tiger waits.

basic_skills.name: Fan of Patience
basic_skills.description: She opens the Tiger's Breath Fan and waves it gently. A soft breeze carries across the battlefield, and all who feel it find their anger cooling, their haste fading, their desire for immediate action replaced by calm consideration.

passive_skill.name: Aura of Eternal Stillness
passive_skill.description: Pokihata radiates an aura of profound patience at all times. All within range feel time moving more slowly, their urgency fading, their impulses becoming manageable. The angry find their rage cooling; the impatient find themselves able to wait; the frantic find stillness. This aura does not suppress action—it simply ensures that when action comes, it is chosen, not compelled.

special_skills.name: Tiger's Wait
special_skills.description: Pokihata dismounts and sits beside Myeongho in perfect stillness. Together, they simply wait. Minutes pass, then hours. Enemies grow confused, then impatient, then careless. They attack, but in their haste they make mistakes. And when the perfect moment arrives—when an enemy is off-balance, overextended, vulnerable—Pokihata extends the Stillness Claw and strikes exactly once. The battle ends.

special_skills.name: Storm's Patience
special_skills.description: She opens the Tiger's Breath Fan wide and spins it slowly. From it, a gentle cyclone of azure mist expands, covering the battlefield. Within the mist, time seems to stretch. Seconds become minutes. The furious find their rage exhausting itself against nothing. When the mist clears, many have simply... stopped fighting. They have had time to think, and they no longer wish to fight.

special_skills.name: Perfect Moment
special_skills.description: Pokihata closes her eyes and enters a trance, seeing all possible futures, all possible moments. When she opens them, she knows exactly when to act. She may wait minutes, hours, days—but when she moves, it is always at the precise instant that guarantees success. The Stillness Claw extends, and one strike ends whatever needs ending.

ultimate_skill.name: Patience's Gift: The Moment That Waited Forever
ultimate_skill.description: Pokihata Bijau's azure eyes blaze with calm light, and Myeongho rises to his full height, his silver stripes glowing. She raises the Tiger's Breath Fan and opens it slowly, deliberately, and from it flows not wind but time itself—slowed, stretched, eternal. She speaks a single, soft word: 'Wait.' In that moment, the entire battlefield freezes—not in physical paralysis, but in a shared experience of patience. Every soul present feels time slow to a crawl. Seconds stretch into hours. The furious feel their rage burning itself out against the endless wait. The hasty feel their urgency becoming absurd. They have all the time in the world to think, to reconsider, to understand. And as they wait, Pokihata walks among them, the Stillness Claw retracted, her eyes calm. She speaks to each one, not in words but in presence, showing them that there is no need to rush, no need to fight, no need to rage. When time finally resumes its normal flow, most have laid down their weapons. Those who haven't face Myeongho, who has been waiting too, and whose patience is now at an end. The tiger strikes exactly once, exactly where needed, and the threat is gone. Pokihata stands at the center, the fan closing with a soft click. She has not defeated her enemies with violence. She has simply waited them out. She is Pokihata Bijau. She is Patience. And she can wait forever.

title: Kindness • The Stag's Heart
lore: In a small fishing village on the coast of Japan, there lived a young woman named Heinki Kuratsa who was known for her extraordinary kindness. She was not wealthy, nor powerful, nor particularly beautiful—yet people traveled from distant villages just to be in her presence. Her gift was simple: she could not bear to see any living thing suffer. She rescued injured birds, calmed frightened children, sat with the dying, and listened to the brokenhearted. Her own heart seemed limitless in its capacity to hold others' pain. One winter, a terrible storm destroyed the village's fishing fleet. Many families lost their fathers, their sons, their livelihood. Heinki went from house to house, not with food or money (she had none), but with presence. She sat with the widows, held the orphans, and whispered words that seemed to come from somewhere beyond her. People said that after she left, the grief was still there, but it was lighter—as if she had carried some of it away with her. A wandering monk came to the village and heard of Heinki. He found her by the shore, feeding an injured seagull from her own meager portion of rice. He watched her for a long time, then approached. 'You give what you do not have,' he said. 'You pour from an empty cup.' Heinki smiled. 'My cup is never empty. Every time I give, it fills again.' The monk revealed himself as Bijuingi Thorak. 'You have the heart of a stag,' he said, 'gentle, protective, nurturing. Will you become Kindness itself, and ride a great stag into battle against Envy? Will you teach the covetous that true wealth is in celebrating others' joy?' Heinki accepted without hesitation. Her simple clothes became a flowing robe of forest green and earth brown silk, embroidered with golden acorns and antlers. Her skin took on a warm, healthy glow. And from the ancient forest nearby stepped a colossal stag, its antlers spreading like the branches of an oak, its coat rich brown with golden dapples, its eyes deep and gentle. It walked to her and bowed its great head. She mounted, and they became one in purpose. Now, Heinki rides her stag through the realms, seeking those twisted by envy, showing them that another's joy does not diminish their own, and that kindness is the only cure for a covetous heart.

Her eyes are large, almond-shaped pools of warm forest brown, holding an eternal, gentle acceptance that makes you feel instantly understood, instantly cherished. When she looks at you, you feel that your pain matters, your joy matters, you matter. Her hair is a magnificent cascade of deep chestnut brown, shot through with subtle golden highlights like sunlight through leaves, falling past her waist in soft, natural waves, often adorned with small acorns and oak leaves woven into the strands. Her attire is a masterpiece of nurturing elegance. She wears a flowing kimono-style robe of forest green silk, overlaid with a lighter robe of earth brown, embroidered with gold thread in patterns of acorns, oak leaves, and grazing stags. The robe is modest yet reveals the graceful contours of her body—the V-neckline shows just a hint of her collarbone and the upper swell of her breasts, while the waist is cinched with a wide belt of woven golden cords, emphasizing her hourglass figure. Over her shoulders, she wears a short cape of soft brown deer hide, lined with green silk, edged with golden acorns. Gold armlets in the shape of intertwined oak leaves adorn her upper arms, and matching anklets circle her delicate ankles. Around her neck, she wears a simple but elegant necklace of gold and amber, with a single, large teardrop amber resting at the hollow of her throat. On her fingers, she wears several gold rings, each set with a small amber stone. On her feet, she wears soft brown leather boots that reach mid-calf, soled for silent walking through forests. In her gentle, capable hands, she carries her legendary weapons: the Antler of Blessing and the Forest Heart Pendant. The Antler of Blessing is a single branch of a stag's antler, wrapped in forest vines and glowing with warm golden light, which when touched to someone amplifies their capacity to celebrate others' joy and heals the wound of envy. The Forest Heart Pendant is a pendant of green crystal shaped like an acorn, which when worn reminds the bearer of their own unique worth—that they need not covet because they are already complete. Beside her always stands her spirit animal and mount: a colossal stag named Moriko. The stag is magnificent, its antlers spreading wider than a wagon, each tine carved with natural runes of kindness. Its coat is rich brown with golden dapples that shift in the light, and its eyes are deep, warm pools of amber. When it moves, it moves with deliberate gentleness, and when it runs, its hooves make no sound on the forest floor. Heinki rides Moriko into battle, and together they are the embodiment of nurturing strength—the stag's antlers can shelter the vulnerable, and its presence calms the envious heart. She is Heinki Kuratsa, and her kindness is not weakness—it is the strongest thing in the world.

story.part1: Heinki's earliest memories are of caring for things smaller than herself. She nursed injured sparrows back to health, shared her food with stray dogs, and comforted crying children. Her parents marveled at her bottomless well of compassion.
story.part2: As she grew, her reputation spread. People came from distant villages just to sit with her, to feel her presence. She had no medicine, no wisdom, no wealth—only the extraordinary gift of making others feel seen and valued.
story.part3: The great storm took everything from her village. Heinki had nothing to give but herself. She went from house to house, sitting with the grieving, holding the frightened, whispering words that seemed to come from somewhere beyond her.
story.part4: After the storm, the village began to heal. People said that Heinki had carried their grief away with her, that her presence made the unbearable bearable. She asked for nothing in return.

The envious feel their bitterness dissolve, replaced by a warm, surprising happiness for others. The lonely feel connected. The resentful feel freed. The antler can also be used to create gentle arcs of golden light that bless entire groups, spreading the warmth of shared joy.
